D397E890DFE30131507868A86D17958E.description: Compose simple shapes to form larger shapes.
comments: For example, "Can you join these two triangles with full sides touching to make a rectangle?"

D397A6D0DFE30131507768A86D17958E.description: Model shapes in the world by building shapes from components (e.g., sticks and clay balls) and drawing shapes.

D3975F30DFE30131507668A86D17958E.description: Analyze and compare two- and three-dimensional shapes, in different sizes and orientations, using informal language to describe their similarities, differences, parts (e.g., number of sides and vertices/"corners") and other attributes (e.g., having sides of equal length).

D3970DC0DFE30131507568A86D17958E.description: Analyze, compare, create, and compose shapes.

D396C9A0DFE30131507468A86D17958E.description: Identify shapes as two-dimensional (lying in a plane, "flat") or three-dimensional ("solid").

D3968200DFE30131507368A86D17958E.description: Correctly name shapes regardless of their orientations or overall size.

D3963760DFE30131507268A86D17958E.description: Describe objects in the environment using names of shapes, and describe the relative positions of these objects using terms such as above, below, beside, in front of, behind, and next to.

D395EE60DFE30131507168A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe shapes (squares, circles, triangles, rectangles, hexagons, cubes, cones, cylinders, and spheres).

D39558F0DFE30131506F68A86D17958E.description: Classify objects into given categories; count the numbers of objects in each category and sort the categories by count.
comments: Limit category counts to be less than or equal to 10.

D3951900DFE30131506E68A86D17958E.description: Classify objects and count the number of objects in each category.

D394D920DFE30131506D68A86D17958E.description: Directly compare two objects with a measurable attribute in common, to see which object has "more of"/"less of" the attribute, and describe the difference.
comments: For example, directly compare the heights of two children and describe one child as taller/shorter.

D3949830DFE30131506C68A86D17958E.description: Describe measurable attributes of objects, such as length or weight. Describe several measurable attributes of a single object.

D393B8E0DFE30131506968A86D17958E.description: Compose and decompose numbers from 11 to 19 into ten ones and some further ones, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record each composition or decomposition by a drawing or equation (e.g., 18 = 10 + 8); understand that these numbers are composed of ten ones and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.

D39375B0DFE30131506868A86D17958E.description: Work with numbers 11—19 to gain foundations for place value.

D3933300DFE30131506768A86D17958E.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten
comments: Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to whole numbers less than or equal to 1,000,000.

D392B1C0DFE30131506568A86D17958E.description: For any number from 1 to 9, find the number that makes 10 when added to the given number, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record the answer with a drawing or equation.

D3926C70DFE30131506468A86D17958E.description: Decompose numbers less than or equal to 10 into pairs in more than one way, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record each decomposition by a drawing or equation (e.g., 5 = 2 + 3 and 5 = 4 + 1).

D3921E70DFE30131506368A86D17958E.description: Solve addition and subtraction word problems, and add and subtract within 10, e.g., by using objects or drawings to represent the problem.

D391CA20DFE30131506268A86D17958E.description: Represent addition and subtraction with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds (e.g., claps), acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations.
comments: Drawings need not show details, but should show the mathematics in the problem (This applies wherever drawings are mentioned in the Standards.)

D3917D60DFE30131506168A86D17958E.description: Understand addition as putting together and adding to, and understand subtraction as taking apart and taking from.

D390E620DFE30131505F68A86D17958E.description: Compare two numbers between 1 and 10 presented as written numerals.

D3909510DFE30131505E68A86D17958E.description: Identify whether the number of objects in one group is greater than, less than, or equal to the number of objects in another group, e.g., by using matching and counting strategies.
comments: Include groups with up to ten objects.

D39000F0DFE30131505C68A86D17958E.description: Count to answer "how many?" questions about as many as 20 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, or a circle, or as many as 10 things in a scattered configuration; given a number from 1—20, count out that many objects.

D38FC060DFE30131505B68A86D17958E.description: Understand that each successive number name refers to a quantity that is one larger.

D38F7D50DFE30131505A68A86D17958E.description: Understand that the last number name said tells the number of objects counted. The number of objects is the same regardless of their arrangement or the order in which they were counted.

D38F3810DFE30131505968A86D17958E.description: When counting objects, say the number names in the standard order, pairing each object with one and only one number name and each number name with one and only one object.

D38EF300DFE30131505868A86D17958E.description: Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities; connect counting to cardinality.

D38EA930DFE30131505768A86D17958E.description: Count to tell the number of objects.

D38E6BA0DFE30131505668A86D17958E.description: Write numbers from 0 to 20. Represent a number of objects with a written numeral 0-20 (with 0 representing a count of no objects).

D38E2AD0DFE30131505568A86D17958E.description: Count forward beginning from a given number within the known sequence (instead of having to begin at 1).

D38DE960DFE30131505468A86D17958E.description: Count to 100 by ones and by tens.

D38DA2C0DFE30131505368A86D17958E.description: Know number names and the count sequence.

D38D1D50DFE30131505168A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

D38CCCB0DFE30131505068A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.

D38BBF90DFE30131504C68A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

D38B3A60DFE30131504A68A86D17958E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

9E63047BCF21495FAB43388987141600.description: With appropriate guidance, explore how context (e.g. social, cultural, and historical) can inform a performance.

E6C4B615F7CC4334A7EB576F0F118529.description: With appropriate guidance, explore relationships between musics and other content areas (e.g. dance, visual art, dramatic arts, literature, science, math, social studies, and language arts).

A60992835BA843F0B440E54833CF6671.description: Relate artistic ideas and works with societal, cultural and historical context to deepen understanding.

6506081717EE4070AA9517B1060C6E43.description: With appropriate guidance, explore various uses of music in daily experiences (e.g. songs of celebration, game songs, marches, T.V., movie, and video game sound tracks, dance music, and work songs).

E5047A0401F84827B139E9A4AFBFB257.description: With appropriate guidance, express personal preferences in music.

6D5F4097948B4245AC83D5E70751A5E7.description: Synthesize and relate knowledge and personal experiences to make art.

7E00DEE319CB443C809AF582BB5FD72E.description: With appropriate guidance, apply teacher-provided criteria to evaluate musical works and performances.

FF8975082F5941D0AA8FD513E63C1B14.description: Apply criteria to evaluate artistic work

29BF87D9B2194D2285399AB8CA2BFD1D.description: With appropriate guidance, identify expressive attributes that reflect creators'/performers' expressive intent (e.g. dynamics).

52CFD41974AA4BED97D0B7A03D9CF669.description: Interpret intent and meaning in artistic work

37B95575C3674B1E94A756BC2D65A3D4.description: With appropriate guidance, demonstrate musical concepts in various styles of music (e.g. beat and pitch).

02A7245A326A4E95921BC962A8AD086C.description: With appropriate guidance, list personal musical interests.

44F22BCA932242E6847C5A164714328B.description: Perform appropriately for the audience and occasion.

D2F7EF66B61E4217AAE413C502D0A6C0.description: With appropriate guidance, perform music with expression (e.g. dynamics).

2C92B11A1AE644BFAF8D3204547B1FAB.description: Convey meaning through the presentation of artistic work

A6C959656E1C435E8CDCB77B3AE50E75.description: With appropriate guidance, use suggested strategies in rehearsal to address interpretive challenges of music.

E37A50E968D446D0A80C7F625A2C0FB0.description: With appropriate guidance, apply personal, teacher, and peer feedback to refine performance.

EC8F881DA0314C56997BCCBF661D8801.description: Develop and refine artistic techniques and work for presentation

7E690CFFDB8F424F90D2538542D02669.description: Explore and describe musical concepts (e.g. voice quality, movement, dynamics, tempo, and melodic contour).

CE7E8F2470624915B4D32D072269AFA5.description: With appropriate guidance, read and perform rhythmic and melodic patterns using notation (e.g. traditional notation).

3DF7D365090040F392B899BE25626D69.description: With appropriate guidance, demonstrate knowledge of musical concepts in music from a variety of cultures selected for performance (e.g. beat and melodic contour).

A201428F87604F0CB73287E1F3DD1C06.description: With appropriate guidance, demonstrate and state personal interest in varied musical selections (e.g. knowledge, purpose).

3BCF2DE4AE0B470D8E33CE8CBDC1F255.description: Select, Analyze and Interpret artistic work for performance

336E6FFCF2984B279CF974A6C00E4B87.description: With appropriate guidance, present a final version of personal or collective musical ideas to peers or informal audience.

5D73D7F116224C5CAF82472468814903.description: With appropriate guidance, discuss and apply personal, peer, and teacher feedback to refine personal musical ideas.

54A82A71209048D0B8445E35504A2C1C.description: With appropriate guidance use notation to document and organize personal or collective musical ideas.

E69984609E7F42A9B6FADA7FAA559B9C.description: With appropriate guidance, demonstrate and discuss personal reasons for selecting musical ideas (e.g. expressive intent).

4909049F9FF3470CA51BB5597B10BDEC.description: Organize and develop artistic ideas and work

B358245B5DC840568997BF9596C2F92B.description: With appropriate guidance, generate musical ideas in multiple tonalities (e.g. major, minor, modal, and pentatonic) and meters (e.g. duple, triple, simple, and compound).

0E70772C7D8C49319D875C5CA064B400.description: With appropriate guidance, improvise musical ideas (e.g. beat, meter, and rhythm).

1569BC1F04134CC28746C8DA0BCEAA8A.description: Generate and conceptualize artistic ideas and work

document.title: Arizona Academic Content Standards Social Studies

DD1429E0DFE30131607768A86D17958E.description: Describe types of personal investments (e.g., saving accounts, stocks, bonds).

DD13E000DFE30131607668A86D17958E.description: Describe how income for most people is determined by the value of the goods and services they sell.

DD138F30DFE30131607568A86D17958E.description: Describe how scarcity influences personal financial choices (e.g., buying on-margin, budgeting, saving, investing, credit).

DD133560DFE30131607468A86D17958E.description: Describe how scarcity influenced the historical times studied.

comments: Decision-making skills foster a person's individual standard of living. Using information wisely leads to better informed decisions as consumers, workers, investors, and effective participants in society.

DD127B60DFE30131607268A86D17958E.description: Identify the patterns of economic interaction (e.g., national debt, balance of trade) between countries.

DD123300DFE30131607168A86D17958E.description: Explain how voluntary exchange benefits buyers and sellers.

comments: Patterns of global interaction and economic development vary due to different economic systems and institutions that exist throughout the world. Since the United States is economically interconnected with the whole world, an understanding of these principles promotes a stronger economy.

DD11A400DFE30131606F68A86D17958E.description: Describe how scarcity influences the choices (e.g., war time rationing, women in the work force, reallocation of resources) made by governments and businesses.

DD115490DFE30131606E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the government's role (e.g., FDIC, Securities and Exchange Commission) in national economic recovery.

DD110030DFE30131606D68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the effects (e.g., inflation, unemployment) of the Great Depression.

DD10B2E0DFE30131606C68A86D17958E.description: Describe the effects of inflation (e.g., higher prices, rising interest rates, less business activity) on society.

comments: Macroeconomics examines the costs and benefits of economic choices made at a societal level and how those choices affect overall economic well being. Understanding of these principles allows the student to recognize the cause and effect of national economic policy.

DD0D9BB0DFE30131606268A86D17958E.description: Describe the government's role in economic recovery for the individual (e.g., farm subsidy, securities, Social Security, exchange regulations).

DD101EC0DFE30131606A68A86D17958E.description: Describe the government's investment in physical capital (e.g., NASA, transportation).

DD0FD620DFE30131606968A86D17958E.description:
Describe the government's investment in human capital:
  1. health
  2. education
  3. training of people

DD0F8550DFE30131606868A86D17958E.description: Explain how the (unequal) distribution of income affects public policy and standards of living.

DD0F2630DFE30131606768A86D17958E.description: Describe how the interaction between buyers and sellers determines market prices.

DD0ECCC0DFE30131606668A86D17958E.description: Describe the function of private business in producing goods and services.

DD0E8270DFE30131606568A86D17958E.description: Describe the role of entrepreneurs (e.g., Carnegie, Ford, Rockefeller, J. P. Morgan, Vanderbilt) in the free enterprise system.

DD0E3770DFE30131606468A86D17958E.description: Describe how investment in physical capital (e.g., factories, machinery, new technology) leads to economic growth.

DD0DEAF0DFE30131606368A86D17958E.description: Describe how (private) investment in human capital such as health (e.g. immunizations), education (e.g., college), and training of people (e.g., on the job experience), leads to economic growth.

DD0D3F10DFE30131606168A86D17958E.description: Identify the functions and relationships among various institutions (e.g., business firms, banks, government agencies, labor unions, corporations) that make up an economic system.

comments: Microeconomics examines the costs and benefits of economic choices relating to individuals, markets and industries, and governmental policies. Understanding this allows individuals to make informed decisions and participate in the economic life of the nation.

DD0CAB00DFE30131605F68A86D17958E.description:
Describe the characteristics of a market economy:
  1. property rights
  2. freedom of enterprise
  3. competition
  4. consumer choice
  5. limited role of government

DD0C6190DFE30131605E68A86D17958E.description: Identify how governments and businesses make choices based on the availability of resources.

DD0C1410DFE30131605D68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how scarcity, opportunity costs, and trade-offs influence decision making.

DD0BC160DFE30131605C68A86D17958E.description: Explain how limited resources and unlimited human wants cause people to choose some things and give up others.

comments: The foundations of economics are the application of basic economic concepts and decision-making skills. This includes scarcity and the different methods of allocation of good and services. Both personal and national decisions are best made with a firm understanding of these principles.

The goal of the economics strand is to enable students to make reasoned judgments about both personal economic questions and broader questions of economic policy. Students will develop an economic way of thinking and problem solving to understand and apply basic economic principles to decisions they will make as consumers, members of the workforce, citizens, voters, and participants in a global marketplace. This will prepare students to weigh both short-term and long-term effects of decisions as well as possible unintended consequences. The study of economics explains historical developments and patterns, the results of trade, and the distribution of income and wealth in local, regional, national, and world economies. Students will be able to analyze current issues and public policies and to understand the complex relationships among economic, political, and cultural systems.

DD0AA350DFE30131605968A86D17958E.description: Use geographic knowledge and skills (e.g., recognizing patterns, mapping, graphing) when discussing current events.

DD0A5AF0DFE30131605868A86D17958E.description: Describe how environments (e.g., Sun Belt, urban areas) influence living conditions.

DD0A12D0DFE30131605768A86D17958E.description: Describe ways geographic features and conditions influence history. (Connect to time periods studied as well as current events.)

comments: Geographic thinking (asking and answering geographic questions) is used to understand spatial patterns of the past and the present, and to plan for the future. The use of geographic analysis is elemental in solving problems and making good decisions.

DD0975A0DFE30131605568A86D17958E.description: Compare different points of view and research on environmental issues (e.g., land use, natural resources, wildlife, biomes).

DD0929D0DFE30131605468A86D17958E.description: Describe the ways human population growth can affect environments and the capacity of environments to support populations.

DD08DD70DFE30131605368A86D17958E.description: Explain how modification in one place (e.g., canals, dams, farming techniques, industrialization) often leads to changes in other locations.

DD089150DFE30131605268A86D17958E.description: Describe the positive and negative outcomes of human modification on the environment.

DD084140DFE30131605168A86D17958E.description: Describe how humans modify environments (e.g., conservation, deforestation, dams) and adapt to the environment.

DD07F030DFE30131605068A86D17958E.description: Describe the consequences of natural hazards (e.g., Dust Bowl hurricanes, droughts, earthquakes).

DD079420DFE30131604F68A86D17958E.description: Identify the physical processes (e.g., conservation of natural resources, mining, water distribution in Arizona) that influence the formation and location of resources.

comments: Human and environmental interactions are interdependent. Humans interact with the environment- they depend upon it, they modify it; and they adapt to it. The health and well-being of all humans depends upon an understanding of the interconnections and interdependence of human and physical systems.

DD05EED0DFE30131604A68A86D17958E.description: Describe the aspects of culture (e.g., literacy, occupations, clothing, property rights) related to beliefs and understandings that influence the economic, social, and political activities of men and women.

DD03E6C0DFE30131604468A86D17958E.description: Describe how changes in technology, transportation, communication, and resources affect the location of economic activities in places and world regions.

DD06F970DFE30131604D68A86D17958E.description: Identify cultural aspects (e.g., literacy rates, occupations, property rights) based on social and political factors.

DD06A1D0DFE30131604C68A86D17958E.description: Explain how cooperation and conflict contribute to political, economic, and social activities.

DD064C30DFE30131604B68A86D17958E.description: Describe the factors (e.g., nearness to transportation routes, markets, raw materials, labor force) that influence the location, distribution and interrelationships of economic activities in different places and world regions.

DD05A3F0DFE30131604968A86D17958E.description: Describe the distributions and patterns of cultural characteristics (e.g., religions, language, standards of living) over time.

DD0553F0DFE30131604868A86D17958E.description: Analyze the effects of settlement (e.g., quality of life, transportation, population density) on places.

DD04E510DFE30131604768A86D17958E.description: Analyze how social (e.g., family), physical (e.g., good climate, farmland, water, minerals), and economic (e.g., jobs) resources influence where human populations choose to live.

DD0487B0DFE30131604668A86D17958E.description: Describe the effects of human migration (e.g., imperialism, quota system, changing of political boundaries, multiculturalism) in the U.S. and regions of the world.

DD042C40DFE30131604568A86D17958E.description: Describe the push and pull factors (e.g., need for raw materials, enslavement, employment opportunities, impact of war, religious freedom, political freedom) that cause human migrations.

DD039E50DFE30131604368A86D17958E.description: Discuss the implications of the demographic structure of places and regions.

comments: Human cultures, their nature, and distribution affect societies and the Earth. The world is increasingly interconnected and these concepts allow full understanding of major issues facing us.

DD030A00DFE30131604168A86D17958E.description: Explain the relationships between the Earth and other objects in the solar system.

DD02BDF0DFE30131604068A86D17958E.description: Relate plate tectonics to the resulting landforms and earthquakes.

DD026B60DFE30131603F68A86D17958E.description: Describe the basic properties of earth materials (rocks, fossils, layers of the earth) and how change over time is estimated.

DD022070DFE30131603E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze relationships in the environment (food chains, food webs, carrying capacity, problems associated with population growth, environmental factors) affecting living organisms.

DD01D830DFE30131603D68A86D17958E.description: Analyze environmental benefits and risks of human interactions.

comments: Physical processes shape the Earth and interact with plant and animal life to create, sustain, and modify ecosystems. These processes affect the distribution of resources and economic development. Science Strands are summarized as they apply to Social Studies content in Grades K-8. In High School, the Performance Objectives are a summary of skills and content for grades 9 -12. These concepts are reinforced in Social Studies classes, but assessed through Science.

DD012F70DFE30131603B68A86D17958E.description: Describe how a place changes over time. (Connect with content studied.)

DD00D780DFE30131603A68A86D17958E.description: Compare the historical and contemporary interactions among people in different places and regions.

DD008810DFE30131603968A86D17958E.description: Explain the concept of regions and why they change.

DD003E20DFE30131603868A86D17958E.description: Describe the human and physical characteristics of places and regions.

comments: Places and regions have distinct physical and cultural characteristics. These concepts are a foundation for many economic, political, and social decisions made throughout the world.

DCFF94E0DFE30131603668A86D17958E.description: Interpret thematic maps, graphs, charts, and databases depicting various aspects of the United States and world regions. (Apply to regions studied.)

DCFF1B00DFE30131603568A86D17958E.description: Locate physical and cultural features (e.g., continents, cities, countries, significant waterways, mountain ranges, climate zones, major water bodies, landforms) throughout the world.

DCFEB690DFE30131603468A86D17958E.description: Interpret maps, charts, and geographic databases using geographic information.

DCFE6340DFE30131603368A86D17958E.description: Identify purposes and differences of maps, globes, aerial photographs, charts, and satellite images.

DCFE1900DFE30131603268A86D17958E.description: Construct maps, charts, and graphs to display geographic information.

comments: The spatial perspective and associated geographic tools are used to organize and interpret information about people, places and environments. Mastery of these tools enables students to better understand information and make decisions that affect the future.

The goal of the geography strand is to provide an understanding of the human and physical characteristics of the Earth's places and regions and how people of different cultural backgrounds interact with their environment. Geographic reasoning is a way of studying human and natural features within a spatial perspective. Through the study of geography, students will be able to understand local, national, regional, and global issues. Students will interpret the arrangement and interactions of human and physical systems on the surface of the Earth. As these patterns have changed over time and are important to governments and economies, geographic reasoning will enhance students' understanding of history, civics, and economics.

DCFCDAE0DFE30131602E68A86D17958E.description: Discuss how negotiations with foreign governments have led to the development of foreign policy initiatives (e.g., Treaty of Versailles, Fourteen Points, League of Nations).

comments: Different governmental systems exist throughout the world. The United States influences and is influenced by global interactions.

DCFC3630DFE30131602C68A86D17958E.description: Describe the impact of Constitutional Amendments and laws (i.e., Thirteenth, Fourteenth, Fifteenth, Eighteenth, Nineteenth, and Twenty-first Amendments, Jim Crow Laws, Black Codes, Dawes Act) that came about during the historical time periods studied.

DCFBDDC0DFE30131602B68A86D17958E.description:
Explain the obligations and responsibilities of citizenship:
  1. upholding the Constitution
  2. obeying the law
  3. paying taxes
  4. registering for selective service
  5. jury duty

DCFB8A80DFE30131602A68A86D17958E.description: Describe the importance of citizens being actively involved in the democratic process (i.e., voting, student government, involvement in political decision making, analyzing issues, petitioning public officials).

DCFB3490DFE30131602968A86D17958E.description: Discuss the character traits (e.g., respect, responsibility, fairness, involvement) that are important to the preservation and improvement of constitutional democracy in the United States

DCFAEAD0DFE30131602868A86D17958E.description: Describe the benefits of community service.

DCFAA1C0DFE30131602768A86D17958E.description: Rights, Responsibilities, and Roles of Citizenship
comments: The rights, responsibilities, and practices of United States citizenship are founded in the Constitution and the nation's history. Fully informed citizens are better able to protect the rights and privileges guaranteed to the citizens of our nation.

DCFA5970DFE30131602668A86D17958E.description: Identify the government's role in progressive reforms (e.g., women's suffrage, labor unions, temperance movement, civil rights).

DCFA0CC0DFE30131602568A86D17958E.description:
Analyze the significance of the following judicial decisions:
  1. Dred Scott
  2. Plessy v. Ferguson
  3. Scopes Trial

comments: Laws and policies are developed to govern, protect, and promote the well-being of the people. Our ever-evolving government sets policies and creates laws to achieve these goals.

DCF95480DFE30131602368A86D17958E.description:
Describe how the powers of checks and balances are used in the following:
  1. impeachment
  2. declaring war
  3. treaties
  4. veto
  5. judicial review

comments: The United States structure of government is characterized by the separation and balance of powers. Participation as an informed citizen requires fundamental knowledge of how our government is structured and the safeguards that are in place to ensure the integrity of the democratic process.

DCF8C770DFE30131602168A86D17958E.description:
Analyze Arizona's transition from territory to statehood:
  1. locations of capital
  2. founding people
  3. Arizona's constitution

DCF87D30DFE30131602068A86D17958E.description:
Analyze the significance of the principles and ideals of the following documents:
  1. Bill of Rights (as related to specific time periods)
  2. Emancipation Proclamation

comments: United States democracy is based on the principles and ideals that are embodied by symbols, people and documents. An understanding of these principles and ideals are vital for citizens to participate fully in the democratic process.

The goal of the civics strand is to develop the requisite knowledge and skills for informed, responsible participation in public life; to ensure, through instruction, that students understand the essentials, source, and history of the constitutions of the United States and Arizona, American institutions and ideals (ARS 15-710). Students will understand the foundations, principles, and institutional practices of the United States as a representative democracy and constitutional republic. They will understand the importance of each person as an individual with human and civil rights and our shared heritage in the United States. Students will understand politics, government, and the responsibilities of good citizenship. Citizenship skills include the capacity to influence policies and decisions by clearly communicating interests and the ability to build coalitions through negotiation, compromise, and consensus. In addition, students will learn that the United States influences and is influenced by global interaction.

DCF786D0DFE30131601D68A86D17958E.description: Compare the economic, political, and social aspects of a country identified in Concept 8 above during the first half of the 20th century to its contemporary economic, political, and social aspects.

DCF741A0DFE30131601C68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how world events of the late 20th century and early 21st century (e.g., terrorism, globalization, conflicts, interdependence, natural disasters, advancements in science and technology, environmental issues) affected, and continue to affect, the social, political, geographic, and economic climate of the world.

DCF6FC10DFE30131601B68A86D17958E.description: Identify the connection between current and historical events and issues identified in Concept 8 above using information from class discussions and various resources (e.g., newspapers, magazines, television, Internet, books, maps).

DCF6B690DFE30131601A68A86D17958E.description: Describe current events using information from class discussions and various resources (e.g., newspapers, magazines, television, Internet, books, maps).

Summarize the outcomes of World War I:
  1. Treaty of Versailles (e.g., restrictions on Germany, end of the Ottoman Empire, redrawing of European boundaries)
  2. economic issues (e.g., national debt, spread of socialism)

Explain how the following world movements led to World War I:
  1. militarism
  2. imperialism
  3. nationalism
  4. formation of alliances

comments: Global events, economic issues, and political ideologies ignited tensions leading to worldwide military conflagrations and diplomatic confrontations in a context of development and change. The changes in the concentration of political power led to changes in the world that continue today.

DCF4EDF0DFE30131601468A86D17958E.description:
Describe the impact of American interests in the following areas during the late 19th century and the early 20th century:

DCF43F50DFE30131601268A86D17958E.description: Describe how areas in the world (e.g., Africa, India, China) were impacted by the imperialism of European countries.

DCF3D500DFE30131601168A86D17958E.description:

  2. increased need for consumers

comments: Industrialized nations exerted political, economic, and social control over less developed areas of the world. The exercise of imperial power led to world tensions that erupted in war and tumultuous change.

  6. labor issues

DCF2FD90DFE30131600E68A86D17958E.description: Describe how innovations and inventions during the Industrial Revolution impacted industry, manufacturing, and transportation.

comments: Intensified internal conflicts led to the radical overthrow of traditional governments and created new political, economic, and intellectual systems. A study of World History is integral for students to analyze the human experience through time, to recognize the relationships of events and people, and to interpret significant patterns, themes, ideas, beliefs, and turning points in American and world history. Students should be able to apply the lessons of World History to their lives as citizens of the United States and members of the world community.

comments: Current events and issues continue to shape our nation and our involvement in the global community. Our role in the world demands informed citizens who know and value the perspective historical knowledge provides.

D3FCF320DFE30131511C68A86D17958E.description: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

D3FCB1C0DFE30131511B68A86D17958E.description: Express whole numbers as fractions, and recognize fractions that are equivalent to whole numbers.
comments: Example: express 3 in the form 3 = 3/1; recognize that 6/1 = 6.
Example: locate 4/4 and 1 at the same point of a number line diagram.

D3FC6F50DFE30131511A68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and generate simple equivalent fractions, e.g., 1/2 = 2/4, 4/6 = 2/3). Explain why the fractions are equivalent, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

D3FC1FE0DFE30131511968A86D17958E.description: Understand two fractions as equivalent (equal) if they are the same size, or the same point on a number line.

D3FBDD60DFE30131511868A86D17958E.description: Explain equivalence of fractions in special cases, and compare fractions by reasoning about their size.

D3FB9DF0DFE30131511768A86D17958E.description: Represent a fraction a/b on a number line diagram by marking off a lengths 1/b from 0. Recognize that the resulting interval has size a/b and that its endpoint locates the number a/b on the number line.

D3FB5CC0DFE30131511668A86D17958E.description: Represent a fraction 1/b on a number line diagram by defining the interval from 0 to 1 as the whole and partitioning it into b equal parts. Recognize that each part has size 1/b and that the endpoint of the part based at 0 locates the number 1/b on the number line.

D3FB1C50DFE30131511568A86D17958E.description: Understand a fraction as a number on the number line; represent fractions on a number line diagram.

D3FAD8C0DFE30131511468A86D17958E.description: Understand a fraction 1/b as the quantity formed by 1 part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts; understand a fraction a/b as the quantity formed by a parts of size 1/b.

D3FA90C0DFE30131511368A86D17958E.description: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers.

comments: Grade 3 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8.
Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 100
For example, partition a shape into 4 parts with equal area, and describe the area of each part as 1/4 of the area of the shape.
D3F9E390DFE30131511168A86D17958E.description: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas. Express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole.

D3F995F0DFE30131511068A86D17958E.description: Understand that shapes in different categories (e.g., rhombuses, rectangles, and others) may share attributes (e.g., having four sides), and that the shared attributes can define a larger category (e.g., quadrilaterals). Recognize rhombuses, rectangles, and squares as examples of quadrilaterals, and draw examples of quadrilaterals that do not belong to any of these subcategories.

D3F95150DFE30131510F68A86D17958E.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

D3F8C260DFE30131510D68A86D17958E.description: Solve real world and mathematical problems involving perimeters of polygons, including finding the perimeter given the side lengths, finding an unknown side length, and exhibiting rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas or with the same area and different perimeters.

D3F86370DFE30131510C68A86D17958E.description: Geometric measurement: recognize perimeter as an attribute of plane figures and distinguish between linear and area measures.

D3F816D0DFE30131510B68A86D17958E.description: Recognize area as additive. Find areas of rectilinear figures by decomposing them into non-overlapping rectangles and adding the areas of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real world problems.

D3F7D3A0DFE30131510A68A86D17958E.description: Use tiling to show in a concrete case that the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths a and b + c is the sum of a × b and a × c. Use area models to represent the distributive property in mathematical reasoning.

D3F79230DFE30131510968A86D17958E.description: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole-number side lengths in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematical reasoning.

D3F75240DFE30131510868A86D17958E.description: Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by tiling it, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths.

D3F710A0DFE30131510768A86D17958E.description: Relate area to the operations of multiplication and addition.

D3F6CE90DFE30131510668A86D17958E.description: Measure areas by counting unit squares (square cm, square m, square in, square ft, and improvised units).

D3F67EE0DFE30131510568A86D17958E.description: A plane figure which can be covered without gaps or overlaps by n unit squares is said to have an area of n square units.

D3F639A0DFE30131510468A86D17958E.description: A square with side length 1 unit, called "a unit square," is said to have "one square unit" of area, and can be used to measure area.

D3F5F2E0DFE30131510368A86D17958E.description: Recognize area as an attribute of plane figures and understand concepts of area measurement.

D3F5A970DFE30131510268A86D17958E.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition.

D3F45B80DFE3013150FE68A86D17958E.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths using rulers marked with halves and fourths of an inch. Show the data by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked off in appropriate units— whole numbers, halves, or quarters.

D3F417B0DFE3013150FD68A86D17958E.description: Draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set with several categories. Solve one- and two-step "how many more" and "how many less" problems using information presented in scaled bar graphs.
comments: For example, draw a bar graph in which each square in the bar graph might represent 5 pets.

D3F55570DFE30131510168A86D17958E.description: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses of objects using standard units of grams (g), kilograms (kg), and liters (l). Add, subtract, multiply, or divide to solve one-step word problems involving masses or volumes that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as a beaker with a measurement scale) to represent the problem.
comments: Excludes multiplicative comparison problems (problems involving notions of "times as much";
Excludes compound units such as cm³ and finding the geometric volume of a container.

D3F4F6A0DFE30131510068A86D17958E.description: Tell and write time to the nearest minute and measure time intervals in minutes. Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals in minutes, e.g., by representing the problem on a number line diagram.

D3F4A160DFE3013150FF68A86D17958E.description: Solve problems involving measurement and estimation of intervals of time, liquid volumes, and masses of objects.

D3F33FE0DFE3013150FA68A86D17958E.description: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of 10 in the range 10—90 (e.g., 9 × 80, 5 × 60) using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.

D3F2F040DFE3013150F968A86D17958E.description: Fluently add and subtract within 1000 using strategies and algorithms based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.

D3F29780DFE3013150F868A86D17958E.description: Use place value understanding to round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.

D3F22A60DFE3013150F768A86D17958E.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.
comments: A range of algorithms may be used.

D3F1DB00DFE3013150F668A86D17958E.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten
comments: Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to whole numbers less than or equal to 1,000,000.

D3F18D10DFE3013150F568A86D17958E.description: Identify arithmetic patterns (including patterns in the addition table or multiplication table), and explain them using properties of operations.
comments: For example, observe that 4 times a number is always even, and explain why 4 times a number can be decomposed into two equal addends.

This standard is limited to problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers; students should know how to perform operations in the conventional order when there are no parentheses to specify a particular order (Order of Operations).
D3F13660DFE3013150F468A86D17958E.description: Solve two-step word problems using the four operations. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.

D3F0DEC0DFE3013150F368A86D17958E.description: Solve problems involving the four operations, and identify and explain patterns in arithmetic.

D3F08780DFE3013150F268A86D17958E.description: Fluently multiply and divide within 100, using strategies such as the relationship between multiplication and division (e.g., knowing that 8 × 5 = 40, one knows 40 ÷ 5 = 8) or properties of operations. By the end of Grade 3, know from memory all products of two one-digit numbers.

D3EFE450DFE3013150F068A86D17958E.description: Understand division as an unknown-factor problem.
comments: For example, find 32 ÷ 8 by finding the number that makes 32 when multiplied by 8.

D3EF8410DFE3013150EF68A86D17958E.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide.
comments: Students need not use formal terms for these properties.
Example: Knowing that 8 × 5 = 40 and 8 × 2 = 16, one can find 8 × 7 as 8 × (5 + 2) = (8 × 5) + (8 × 2) = 40 + 16 = 56. (Distributive property.)

Example: If 6 × 4 = 24 is known, then 4 × 6 = 24 is also known (Commutative property of multiplication.) 3 × 5 × 2 can be found by 3 × 5 = 15, then 15 × 2 = 30, or by 5 × 2 = 10, then 3 × 10 = 30. (Associative property of multiplication.)

D3EF3570DFE3013150EE68A86D17958E.description: Understand properties of multiplication and the relationship between multiplication and division.

For example, describe a context in which a total number of objects can be expressed as 5 × 7.

DCD06530DFE301315FD868A86D17958E.description: Describe the factors lenders consider before lending money.

DCD01C60DFE301315FD768A86D17958E.description: Explain how interest is the price paid to borrow money.

DCCFCAA0DFE301315FD668A86D17958E.description: Compare the cost and benefits of using credit.

comments: Decision-making skills foster a person's individual standard of living. Using information wisely leads to better informed decisions as consumers, workers, investors, and effective participants in society.

DCCF15B0DFE301315FD468A86D17958E.description: Explain how trade promoted economic growth throughout world regions.

DCCEAB10DFE301315FD368A86D17958E.description: Compare how money, as opposed to barter, facilitates trade.

DCCE38C0DFE301315FD268A86D17958E.description: Explain why specialization improves standards of living.

DCCDDC60DFE301315FD168A86D17958E.description: Determine how scarcity, opportunity costs, and trade-offs influence decision-making.

DCCD94D0DFE301315FD068A86D17958E.description: Identify how limited resources and unlimited human wants cause people to choose some things and give up others.

comments: The foundations of economics are the application of basic economic concepts and decision-making skills. This includes scarcity and the different methods of allocation of good and services. Both personal and national decisions are best made with a firm understanding of these principles.

The goal of the economics strand is to enable students to make reasoned judgments about both personal economic questions and broader questions of economic policy. Students will develop an economic way of thinking and problem solving to understand and apply basic economic principles to decisions they will make as consumers, members of the workforce, citizens, voters, and participants in a global marketplace. This will prepare students to weigh both short-term and long-term effects of decisions as well as possible unintended consequences. The study of economics explains historical developments and patterns, the results of trade, and the distribution of income and wealth in local, regional, national, and world economies. Students will be able to analyze current issues and public policies and to understand the complex relationships among economic, political, and cultural systems.

DCCCB4C0DFE301315FCD68A86D17958E.description: Use geographic knowledge and skills (e.g., recognizing patterns, mapping, graphing) when discussing current events.

DCCC67A0DFE301315FCC68A86D17958E.description: Describe ways geographic features and conditions influenced settlement in various locations (e.g., near waterways, on high terrain, with adequate fresh water, on good land for farming, in temperate climates) throughout different periods of time, places, and regions.

comments: Geographic thinking (asking and answering geographic questions) is used to understand spatial patterns of the past and the present, and to plan for the future. The use of geographic analysis is elemental in solving problems and making good decisions.

DCCBBA80DFE301315FCA68A86D17958E.description: Identify the way humans respond to/prepare for natural hazards (i.e., lightning, flash floods, dust storms, tornadoes, hurricanes, floods, earthquakes) in order to remain safe.

DCCB63E0DFE301315FC968A86D17958E.description: Explain how changes in the natural environment (e.g., flooding of the Nile) can increase or diminish its capacity to support human activities.

DCCB1960DFE301315FC868A86D17958E.description: Describe the intended and unintended consequences of human modification (e.g., irrigation, aqueducts, canals) on the environment.

DCCACE90DFE301315FC768A86D17958E.description: Describe ways that human dependence on natural resources influences economic development, settlement, trade, and migration.

comments: Human and environmental interactions are interdependent. Humans interact with the environment- they depend upon it, they modify it; and they adapt to it. The health and well-being of all humans depends upon an understanding of the interconnections and interdependence of human and physical systems.

DCCA2D40DFE301315FC568A86D17958E.description: Describe the aspects of culture (e.g., literacy, occupations, clothing, property rights) related to beliefs and understandings that influence the economic, social, and political activities of men and women.

DCC9E880DFE301315FC468A86D17958E.description: Identify cultural norms that influence different social, political, and economic activities of men and women.

DCC99F30DFE301315FC368A86D17958E.description: Identify how factors such as river/coastal civilizations and trade influenced the location, distribution, and interrelationships of economic activities over time and in different regions.

DCC94E80DFE301315FC268A86D17958E.description: Analyze the causes and effects of settlement patterns.

DCC8F080DFE301315FC168A86D17958E.description: Describe the environmental, economic, cultural, and political effects of human migrations and cultural diffusion on places and regions.

DCC8A790DFE301315FC068A86D17958E.description: Interpret the demographic structure of places and regions using a population pyramid.

comments: Human cultures, their nature, and distribution affect societies and the Earth. The world is increasingly interconnected and these concepts allow full understanding of major issues facing us.

DCC811B0DFE301315FBE68A86D17958E.description: Explain the water cycle and factors that affect climate.

DCC7C480DFE301315FBD68A86D17958E.description: Describe the composition of and interactions between bodies of water and the atmosphere.

DCC77B90DFE301315FBC68A86D17958E.description: Describe how sunlight, water quality, climate, population density and pollution affect quality of life.

DCC736E0DFE301315FBB68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the effects of, and describe how people plan for and respond to natural disasters.

DCC6E060DFE301315FBA68A86D17958E.description: Identify the physical processes that influence the formation and location of resources such as oil, coal, diamonds, and copper.

comments: Physical processes shape the Earth and interact with plant and animal life to create, sustain, and modify ecosystems. These processes affect the distribution of resources and economic development. Science Strands are summarized as they apply to Social Studies content in Grades K-8. In High School, the Performance Objectives are a summary of skills and content for grades 9 -12. These concepts are reinforced in Social Studies classes, but assessed through Science.

DCC62AE0DFE301315FB868A86D17958E.description: Describe the physical and human characteristics of places and regions of a Middle Eastern country studied.

DCC5E790DFE301315FB768A86D17958E.description: Explain why places and regions serve as cultural symbols such as Jerusalem being a sacred place for Jews, Christians, and Muslims.

DCC5A480DFE301315FB668A86D17958E.description: Describe the interactions of people in different places and regions.

DCC55FF0DFE301315FB568A86D17958E.description: Describe the factors that cause regions and places to change.

DCC51930DFE301315FB468A86D17958E.description: Identify regions studied in Strand 2 using a variety of criteria (e.g., climate, landforms, culture, vegetation).

comments: Places and regions have distinct physical and cultural characteristics. These concepts are a foundation for many economic, political, and social decisions made throughout the world.

DCC48110DFE301315FB268A86D17958E.description: Interpret thematic maps, graphs, charts, and databases depicting various aspects of world regions. (Apply to regions studied).

DCC43BB0DFE301315FB168A86D17958E.description: Locate physical and human features (e.g., significant waterways, mountain ranges, cities, countries) in the United States and in regions of the world on a map.

DCC3EFA0DFE301315FB068A86D17958E.description: Interpret maps, charts, and geographic databases using geographic information.

DCC38540DFE301315FAF68A86D17958E.description: Identify purposes of, and differences among, maps, globes, aerial photographs, charts, and satellite images.

DCC32980DFE301315FAE68A86D17958E.description: Construct maps, charts, and graphs to display geographic information.

comments: The spatial perspective and associated geographic tools are used to organize and interpret information about people, places and environments. Mastery of these tools enables students to better understand information and make decisions that affect the future.

The goal of the geography strand is to provide an understanding of the human and physical characteristics of the Earth's places and regions and how people of different cultural backgrounds interact with their environment. Geographic reasoning is a way of studying human and natural features within a spatial perspective. Through the study of geography, students will be able to understand local, national, regional, and global issues. Students will interpret the arrangement and interactions of human and physical systems on the surface of the Earth. As these patterns have changed over time and are important to governments and economies, geographic reasoning will enhance students' understanding of history, civics, and economics.

DCC24470DFE301315FAB68A86D17958E.description:
Describe the structure of the following governments:
  1. theocracy
  2. dictatorship
  3. republic
  4. monarchy
  5. democracy
  6. anarchy

comments: Different governmental systems exist throughout the world. The United States influences and is influenced by global interactions.

DCC1BD10DFE301315FA968A86D17958E.description: Describe the importance of citizens being actively involved in the democratic process (e.g., voting, student government, involvement in political decision making, analyzing issues, petitioning public officials).

DCC17860DFE301315FA868A86D17958E.description: Discuss the character traits (i.e., respect, responsibility, fairness, involvement) that are important to the preservation and improvement of constitutional democracy in the United States.

DCC12BA0DFE301315FA768A86D17958E.description: Describe ways an individual can contribute to a school or community.

DCC0D360DFE301315FA668A86D17958E.description: Rights, Responsibilities, and Roles of Citizenship
comments: The rights, responsibilities, and practices of United States citizenship are founded in the Constitution and the nation's history. Fully informed citizens are better able to protect the rights and privileges guaranteed to the citizens of our nation.

DCC08F60DFE301315FA568A86D17958E.description: Describe the impact of the Roman republic on ancient Romans and how it relates to current forms of government.

DCC04C10DFE301315FA468A86D17958E.description: Describe the impact of the Greek democracy on ancient Greeks and how it relates to current forms of government.

DCC00700DFE301315FA368A86D17958E.description: Describe the impact of the Laws of Hammurabi on the lives of ancient people and how it relates to current laws.

comments: Laws and policies are developed to govern, protect, and promote the well-being of the people. Our ever-evolving government sets policies and creates laws to achieve these goals.

DCBF7250DFE301315FA168A86D17958E.description:
Analyze the significance of the principles and ideals of the following documents:
  1. Bill of Rights (as related to specific time periods)
  2. Emancipation Proclamation

DCBF14B0DFE301315FA068A86D17958E.description: Discuss the important ideas of the Enlightenment Period (e.g., Natural Rights, separation of powers, religious freedom) that fostered the creation of the United States government.

comments: United States democracy is based on the principles and ideals that are embodied by symbols, people and documents. An understanding of these principles and ideals are vital for citizens to participate fully in the democratic process.

The goal of the civics strand is to develop the requisite knowledge and skills for informed, responsible participation in public life; to ensure, through instruction, that students understand the essentials, source, and history of the constitutions of the United States and Arizona, American institutions and ideals (ARS 15-710). Students will understand the foundations, principles, and institutional practices of the United States as a representative democracy and constitutional republic. They will understand the importance of each person as an individual with human and civil rights and our shared heritage in the United States. Students will understand politics, government, and the responsibilities of good citizenship. Citizenship skills include the capacity to influence policies and decisions by clearly communicating interests and the ability to build coalitions through negotiation, compromise, and consensus. In addition, students will learn that the United States influences and is influenced by global interaction.

DCBE09B0DFE301315F9D68A86D17958E.description: Identify the connection between current and historical events and issues using information from class discussions and various resources (e.g., newspapers, magazines, television, Internet, books, maps).

DCBDBD80DFE301315F9C68A86D17958E.description: Describe current events using information from class discussions and various resources (e.g., newspapers, magazines, television, Internet, books, maps).

comments: The nations of the contemporary world are shaped by their cultural and political past. Current events, developments, and issues continue to shape the global community.

  2. natural rights (i.e., life, liberty, property)
  3. governmental separation of powers vs. monarchy
  4. religious freedom
  5. Magna Carta

comments: Innovations, discoveries, exploration, and colonization accelerated contact, conflict, and interconnection among societies worldwide, transforming and creating nations. The expansion of the existing nations of the world led to the exchange of ideas, goods, and cultures that formed a foundation for the modern age.

  2. Michelangelo
  3. Gutenberg
  4. Martin Luther

  2. new ideas and products as a result of trade
  3. the arts
  4. science

comments: The rise of individualism challenged traditional Western authority and belief systems resulting in a variety of new institutions, philosophical and religious ideas, and cultural and social achievements. The ideas born in this era continue to form a basis for political and social thought.

DCBB6C50DFE301315F9468A86D17958E.description: Describe how trade routes led to the exchange of ideas (e.g., religion, scientific advances, literature) between Europe, Asia, Africa and the Middle East during the 15th and 16th centuries.

DCBAE790DFE301315F9268A86D17958E.description: Describe the transition from feudalism to nationalism at the end of the Middle Ages.

DCB9A3F0DFE301315F8E68A86D17958E.description: Describe aspects (e.g., geographic origins, founders and their teachings, traditions, customs, beliefs) of Hinduism, Buddhism, Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.

comments: People of different regions developed unique civilizations and cultural identities characterized by increased interaction, societal complexity, cooperation and competition. Examination of these civilizations provides understanding of their enduring contributions to the modern world.

DCB82160DFE301315F8968A86D17958E.description:

  2. Egypt (i.e., mummification, hieroglyphs, papyrus)
  3. China (i.e., silk, gun powder/fireworks, compass)
  4. Central and South America (i.e., astronomy, agriculture)

DCB7D9C0DFE301315F8868A86D17958E.description:
Describe the religious traditions that helped shape the culture of the following ancient civilizations:

  4. Middle East (i.e., monotheism)

DCB796B0DFE301315F8768A86D17958E.description:
Compare the forms of government of the following ancient civilizations:

  3. China – dynasty

DCB67250DFE301315F8368A86D17958E.description: Describe the lifestyles of humans in the Paleolithic and Neolithic Ages.

comments: The geographic, political, economic, and cultural characteristics of early civilizations significantly influenced the development of later civilizations. An understanding of the earliest contributions to society is vital to understanding the rest of the world and our place in it.

comments: Historical research is a process in which students examine topics or questions related to historical studies and/or current issues. document.title: Arizona College and Career Ready Standards – Mathematics

D421B880DFE30131515F68A86D17958E.description: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two decimals refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual model.

D4215EC0DFE30131515E68A86D17958E.description: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 or 100.
comments: For example, rewrite 0.62 as 62/100; describe a length as 0.62 meters; locate 0.62 on a number line diagram.

Students who can generate equivalent fractions can develop strategies for adding fractions with unlike denominators in general. But addition and subtraction with unlike denominators in general is not a requirement at this grade.
For example, express 3/10 as 30/100, and add 3/10 + 4/100 = 34/100.
D4211A20DFE30131515D68A86D17958E.description: Express a fraction with denominator 10 as an equivalent fraction with denominator 100, and use this technique to add two fractions with respective denominators 10 and 100.

D420D8F0DFE30131515C68A86D17958E.description: Understand decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal fractions.

D4209450DFE30131515B68A86D17958E.description: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.
comments: For example, if each person at a party will eat 3/8 of a pound of roast beef, and there will be 5 people at the party, how many pounds of roast beef will be needed? Between what two whole numbers does your answer lie?

D4204D30DFE30131515A68A86D17958E.description: Understand a multiple of a/b as a multiple of 1/b, and use this understanding to multiply a fraction by a whole number.
comments: For example, use a visual fraction model to express 3 × (2/5) as 6 × (1/5), recognizing this product as 6/5. (In general, n × (a/b) = (n × a)/b.)

D4200160DFE30131515968A86D17958E.description: Understand a fraction a/b as a multiple of 1/b.
comments: For example, use a visual fraction model to represent 5/4 as the product 5 × (1/4), recording the conclusion by the equation 5/4 = 5 × (1/4).

D41FB570DFE30131515868A86D17958E.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction by a whole number.

D41F73E0DFE30131515768A86D17958E.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole and having like denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

D41F3160DFE30131515668A86D17958E.description: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators, e.g., by replacing each mixed number with an equivalent fraction, and/or by using properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.

D41EE970DFE30131515568A86D17958E.description: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way, recording each decomposition by an equation. Justify decompositions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

D41EA190DFE30131515468A86D17958E.description: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole.

D41E5160DFE30131515368A86D17958E.description: Understand a fraction a/b with a > 1 as a sum of fractions 1/b.

D41DF2C0DFE30131515268A86D17958E.description: Build fractions from unit fractions by applying and extending previous understandings of operations on whole numbers.

D41DA450DFE30131515168A86D17958E.description: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators, e.g., by creating common denominators or numerators, or by comparing to a benchmark fraction such as 1/2. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

D41D5200DFE30131515068A86D17958E.description: Explain why a fraction a/b is equivalent to a fraction (n × a)/(n × b) by using visual fraction models, with attention to how the number and size of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size. Use this principle to recognize and generate equivalent fractions.

D41D0D00DFE30131514F68A86D17958E.description: Extend understanding of fraction equivalence and ordering.

comments: Grade 3 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8.
Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 100

D41C7E80DFE30131514D68A86D17958E.description: Recognize a line of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure as a line across the figure such that the figure can be folded along the line into matching parts. Identify line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.

D41C1660DFE30131514C68A86D17958E.description: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size. Recognize right triangles as a category, and identify right triangles.

D41BAC70DFE30131514B68A86D17958E.description: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures.

D41B5980DFE30131514A68A86D17958E.description: Draw and identify lines and angles, and classify shapes by properties of their lines and angles.

D41AD2B0DFE30131514868A86D17958E.description: Recognize angle measure as additive. When an angle is decomposed into non-overlapping parts, the angle measure of the whole is the sum of the angle measures of the parts. Solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles on a diagram in real world and mathematical problems, e.g., by using an equation with a symbol for the unknown angle measure.

D41A8AC0DFE30131514768A86D17958E.description: Measure angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor. Sketch angles of specified measure.

D41A38E0DFE30131514668A86D17958E.description: An angle that turns through n one-degree angles is said to have an angle measure of n degrees.

D419F5E0DFE30131514568A86D17958E.description: An angle is measured with reference to a circle with its center at the common endpoint of the rays, by considering the fraction of the circular arc between the points where the two rays intersect the circle. An angle that turns through 1/360 of a circle is called a "one-degree angle," and can be used to measure angles.

D419B170DFE30131514468A86D17958E.description: Recognize angles as geometric shapes that are formed wherever two rays share a common endpoint, and understand concepts of angle measurement:

D4196E70DFE30131514368A86D17958E.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of angle and measure angles.

comments: For example, from a line plot find and interpret the difference in length between the longest and shortest specimens in an insect collection.
D417D480DFE30131513E68A86D17958E.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (1/2, 1/4, 1/8). Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions by using information presented in line plots.

D41926E0DFE30131514268A86D17958E.description: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real world and mathematical problems.
comments: For example, find the width of a rectangular room given the area of the flooring and the length, by viewing the area formula as a multiplication equation with an unknown factor.

D418C4D0DFE30131514168A86D17958E.description: Use the four operations to solve word problems involving distances, intervals of time, liquid volumes, masses of objects, and money, including problems involving simple fractions or decimals, and problems that require expressing measurements given in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Represent measurement quantities using diagrams such as number line diagrams that feature a measurement scale.

D4186A50DFE30131514068A86D17958E.description: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system of units including km, m, cm; kg, g; lb, oz.; l, ml; hr, min, sec. Within a single system of measurement, express measurements in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Record measurement equivalents in a two column table.
comments: For example, know that 1 ft is 12 times as long as 1 in. Express the length of a 4 ft snake as 48 in. Generate a conversion table for feet and inches listing the number pairs (1, 12), (2, 24), (3, 36), …

D4181990DFE30131513F68A86D17958E.description: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of measurements from a larger unit to a smaller unit.

D415C7F0DFE30131513768A86D17958E.description: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

D4158450DFE30131513668A86D17958E.description: Multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit whole number, and multiply two two-digit numbers, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

D4153D40DFE30131513568A86D17958E.description: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.

D414E9F0DFE30131513468A86D17958E.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

D416FDC0DFE30131513B68A86D17958E.description: Use place value understanding to round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.

D416A5D0DFE30131513A68A86D17958E.description: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form. Compare two multi-digit numbers based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

D4165930DFE30131513968A86D17958E.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right.
comments: For example, recognize that 700 ÷ 70 = 10 by applying concepts of place value and division.

D4160B50DFE30131513868A86D17958E.description: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers.

comments: Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to whole numbers less than or equal to 1,000,000.
D414A430DFE30131513368A86D17958E.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

D4146040DFE30131513268A86D17958E.description: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule. Identify apparent features of the pattern that were not explicit in the rule itself.
comments: For example, given the rule "Add 3" and the starting number 1, generate terms in the resulting sequence and observe that the terms appear to alternate between odd and even numbers. Explain informally why the numbers will continue to alternate in this way.

D413CC30DFE30131513068A86D17958E.description: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range 1—100. Recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1—100 is a multiple of a given one-digit number. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1—100 is prime or composite.

D4137730DFE30131512F68A86D17958E.description: Gain familiarity with factors and multiples.

D4132440DFE30131512E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze relationships among representations and make connections to the multiplication principle of counting.

D412E060DFE30131512D68A86D17958E.description: Represent a variety of counting problems using arrays, charts, and systematic lists, e.g., tree diagram.

D412A180DFE30131512C68A86D17958E.description: Solve a variety of problems based on the multiplication principle of counting.

D41260B0DFE30131512B68A86D17958E.description: Solve multistep word problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers using the four operations, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.

D4121F50DFE30131512A68A86D17958E.description: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem, distinguishing multiplicative comparison from additive comparison.

D411DA60DFE30131512968A86D17958E.description: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison, e.g., interpret 35 = 5 × 7 as a statement that 35 is 5 times as many as 7 and 7 times as many as 5. Represent verbal statements of multiplicative comparisons as multiplication equations.

D4117F10DFE30131512868A86D17958E.description: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems.

D410F2F0DFE30131512668A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

D41097F0DFE30131512568A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.

D40F30E0DFE30131512168A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

D40E9180DFE30131511F68A86D17958E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Arizona College and Career Ready Standards – Mathematics

D3D935F0DFE3013150DD68A86D17958E.description: Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, thirds, half of, a third of, etc., and describe the whole as two halves, three thirds, four fourths. Recognize that equal shares of identical wholes need not have the same shape.

D3D8E810DFE3013150DC68A86D17958E.description: Partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and count to find the total number of them.

D3D88FC0DFE3013150DB68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and draw shapes having specified attributes, such as a given number of angles or a given number of equal faces. Identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons, and cubes.
comments: Sizes are compared directly or visually, not compared by measuring.

D3D81C70DFE3013150DA68A86D17958E.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

D3D467F0DFE3013150CC68A86D17958E.description: Draw a picture graph and a bar graph (with single-unit scale) to represent a data set with up to four categories. Solve simple put-together, take-apart, and compare problems using information presented in a bar graph.

D3D4B750DFE3013150CD68A86D17958E.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths of several objects to the nearest whole unit, or by making repeated measurements of the same object. Show the measurements by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked off in whole-number units.

comments: Example: If you have 2 dimes and 3 pennies, how many cents do you have?
D3D792A0DFE3013150D868A86D17958E.description: Solve word problems involving dollar bills, quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies, using $ and ¢ symbols appropriately.

D3D75380DFE3013150D768A86D17958E.description: Tell and write time from analog and digital clocks to the nearest five minutes, using a.m. and p.m.

D3D6D4B0DFE3013150D568A86D17958E.description: Represent whole numbers as lengths from 0 on a number line diagram with equally spaced points corresponding to the numbers 0, 1, 2, …, and represent whole-number sums and differences within 100 on a number line diagram.

D3D692D0DFE3013150D468A86D17958E.description: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve word problems involving lengths that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as drawings of rulers) and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

D3D63CB0DFE3013150D368A86D17958E.description: Relate addition and subtraction to length.

D3D5FDC0DFE3013150D268A86D17958E.description: Measure to determine how much longer one object is than another, expressing the length difference in terms of a standard length unit.

D3D5C020DFE3013150D168A86D17958E.description: Estimate lengths using units of inches, feet, centimeters, and meters.

D3D58060DFE3013150D068A86D17958E.description: Measure the length of an object twice, using length units of different lengths for the two measurements; describe how the two measurements relate to the size of the unit chosen.

D3D54020DFE3013150CF68A86D17958E.description: Measure the length of an object by selecting and using appropriate tools such as rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks, and measuring tapes.

D3D4FD20DFE3013150CE68A86D17958E.description: Measure and estimate lengths in standard units.

comments: Explanations may be supported by drawings or objects.
D3D37DF0DFE3013150C968A86D17958E.description: Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work, using place value and the properties of operations.

D3D33850DFE3013150C868A86D17958E.description: Mentally add 10 or 100 to a given number 100—900, and mentally subtract 10 or 100 from a given number 100—900.

D3D2E8B0DFE3013150C768A86D17958E.description: Add and subtract within 1000, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method. Understand that in adding or subtracting three-digit numbers, one adds or subtracts hundreds and hundreds, tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose or decompose tens or hundreds.

D3D287B0DFE3013150C668A86D17958E.description: Add up to four two-digit numbers using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.

D3D21F90DFE3013150C568A86D17958E.description: Fluently add and subtract within 100 using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.

D3D1D970DFE3013150C468A86D17958E.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.

D3D189F0DFE3013150C368A86D17958E.description: Compare two three-digit numbers based on meanings of the hundreds, tens, and ones digits, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

D3D13E10DFE3013150C268A86D17958E.description: Read and write numbers to 1000 using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form.

D3D0B440DFE3013150C068A86D17958E.description: The numbers 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine hundreds (and 0 tens and 0 ones).

D3D07630DFE3013150BF68A86D17958E.description: 100 can be thought of as a bundle of ten tens — called a "hundred."

D3D03680DFE3013150BE68A86D17958E.description: Understand that the three digits of a three-digit number represent amounts of hundreds, tens, and ones; e.g., 706 equals 7 hundreds, 0 tens, and 6 ones. Understand the following as special cases:

comments: Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to whole numbers less than or equal to 1,000,000.
D3CFB110DFE3013150BC68A86D17958E.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten
