51482197BA0940229D9E5490A18819EB.description: Given a description of a situation, generate a function to model a linear relationship between two quantities. Determine the rate of change and initial value of the function from a description of a relationship or from two (x, y) values, including reading these from a table or a graph. Track how the values of the two quantities change together. Interpret the rate of change and initial value of a linear function in terms of the situation it models, its graph, or its table of values.

DE173AA1E9E04433A2E39E882A223A9B.description: Use functions to model relationships between quantities.

845165E42DCF49AEB34370690F754A11.description: Interpret the equation y = mx + b as defining a linear function whose graph is a straight line; give examples of functions that are not linear.

B314E70E2AC54FFB953F6A563D72EA2C.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).

81A80757EC764D3DB5D052A049FA71EA.description: Understand that a function is a rule that assigns to each input exactly one output. The graph of a function is the set of ordered pairs consisting of an input and the corresponding output. (Function notation is not required in Grade 8.)

16F37EBF805D456FA5A94AB23291CC7F.description: Solve mathematical problems and problems in real-world context leading to two linear equations in two variables.

5F6A34AFB1BC43A89A2E2900D80A18BF.description: Solve systems of two linear equations in two variables algebraically, and estimate solutions by graphing the equations including cases of no solution and infinite number of solutions. Solve simple cases by inspection.

FCDA9432F05341B6A8774F59DDC9185F.description: Understand that solutions to a system of two linear equations in two variables correspond to points of intersection of their graphs, because points of intersection satisfy both equations simultaneously.

FF96F859CB1E4CD7AF40A3C9928B1F92.description: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

869ED42C46E14C67868C4BC0ECDF468A.description: Solve linear equations and inequalities with rational number coefficients, including solutions that require expanding expressions using the distributive property and collecting like terms.

4F809BA424984EAAB21A92A0B5434683.description: Give examples of linear equations in one variable with one solution, infinitely many solutions, or no solution. Show which of these possibilities is the case by successively transforming the given equation into simpler forms, until an equivalent equation of the form x = a, a = a, or a = b results (where a and b are different numbers).

A7E3ED063F8F454BBE75A9748568CDEE.description: Fluently solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable.

0F0D7252D82043B093F2E1FB64B5D023.description: Analyze and solve linear equations, inequalities, and pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

EA200760C34442769198E98D90704446.description: Use similar triangles to explain why the slope m is the same between any two distinct points on a non-vertical line in the coordinate plane. Derive the equation y = mx for a line through the origin and the equation y = mx + b for a line intercepting the vertical axis at (0, b).

94B6A2186464469F967291E4335DD6EC.description: Graph proportional relationships interpreting the unit rate as the slope of the graph. Compare two different proportional relationships represented in different ways.

1F557FDEF49D4B19AA0C5FF2CE6EDBD8.description: Understand the connections between proportional relationships, lines, and linear equations.

7DC0F0CF459444EEB4F42657B37E3740.description: Perform operations with numbers expressed in scientific notation including problems where both decimal and scientific notation are used. Use scientific notation and choose units of appropriate size for measurements of very large or very small quantities.

22522260CF6F406C9650720F9FA337C9.description: Use numbers expressed in the form of a single digit times an integer power of 10 to estimate very large or very small quantities, and express how many times larger or smaller one is than the other.

D473936BC279467B871B3CCEDBDF3704.description: Evaluate cube roots of perfect cubes less than or equal to 1000.

1C1F564730E941E1B046924E495BF7E1.description: Evaluate square roots of perfect squares less than or equal to 225.

AA8C4E92EEB44B1AA3581988521895C5.description: Use square root and cube root symbols to represent solutions to equations of the form x² = p and x³= p, where p is a positive rational number. Know that √2 is irrational.

DCC9D98824244EE4A24DB9FDDA28C312.description: Understand and apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical expressions.

04BCF56708574060BFEEC9249999DFA0.description: Work with radicals and integer exponents.

9FB4217FF3664724ADE0CD426BA2F684.description: Understand that given any two distinct rational numbers, a < b, there exist a rational number c and an irrational number d such that a < c < b and a < d < b. Given any two distinct irrational numbers, a < b, there exist a rational number c and an irrational number d such that a < c < b and a < d < b.

289030D1265A4E20BD81807CE59F0C0C.description: Use rational approximations of irrational numbers to compare the size of irrational numbers. Locate them approximately on a number line diagram, and estimate their values.

5A39C9AB553A4353B58B0C917D86AA1F.description: Know that numbers that are not rational are called irrational. Understand informally that every number has a decimal expansion. Know that numbers whose decimal expansions do not terminate in zeros or in a repeating sequence of fixed digits are called irrational.

2D0AEBB79A594B63A2012D34C1767669.description: Understand that there are irrational numbers, and approximate them using rational numbers.

430AF4C1DE464F00869AE8E447F33918.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

632D1DA3D99F4B7E8D8F5EB4ABC78856.description: Look for and make use of structure.

0712841F5C3C4B43A4BB46F2ACF279D3.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

943E7E59F74B43FBA9D8DD3624548547.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

1268114470F24624AD2F2428EA008804.description: Relating the choice of measures of center and variability to the shape of the data distribution and the context in which the data were gathered.

4C90AA0A2D3A4F6A8FC07B6ECFC60D30.description: Giving quantitative measures of center (median and/or mean) and variability (interquartile range and/or mean absolute deviation), as well as describing any overall pattern and any striking deviations from the overall pattern with reference to the context in which the data were gathered.

AF8E600A4E1C447CA786C0311AC389C9.description: Describing the nature of the attribute under investigation including how it was measured and its units of measurement.

A738919C2B134DF6BD2E7A4DCA2C2F19.description: Summarize numerical data sets in relation to their context by:

08726973873849338D65AEFD6F41B66F.description: Display and interpret numerical data by creating plots on a number line including histograms, dot plots, and box plots.

53AEE8B5F7554B10BBC258B88BD3F7D8.description: Recognize that a measure of center for a numerical data set summarizes all of its values with a single number, while a measure of variation uses a single number to describe the spread of the data set.

6D35EF49455B44229D65A08AB48B1958.description: Understand that a set of data collected to answer a statistical question has a distribution whose general characteristics can be described by its center, spread, and overall shape.

A38ACA4237AD4450B5CC87D6DAF0F5FE.description: Recognize a statistical question as one that anticipates variability in the data related to the question and accounts for variability in the answers.

C2DA09AF9CB24692AB2B9B8D347A3EA1.description: Represent three-dimensional figures using nets made up of rectangles and triangles, and use the nets to find the surface area of these figures. Apply these techniques to solve mathematical problems and problems in real-world context.

03834A3830FC43948C8BF19BBB0079FB.description: Draw polygons in the coordinate plane given coordinates for the vertices; use coordinates to find the length of a side joining points with the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate. Apply these techniques to solve mathematical problems and problems in a real-world context.

17D86DEFA0A84C7BA1A75D01937C756F.description: Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with fractional edge lengths by packing it with unit cubes of the appropriate unit fraction edge lengths, and show that the volume is the same as would be found by multiplying the edge lengths of the prism. Understand and use the formula V = B · h, where in this case, B is the area of the base (B = l × w) to find volumes of right rectangular prisms with fractional edge lengths in mathematical problems and problems in real-world context.

2521FFC45BF749518BE222B720E3A066.description: Find the area of right triangles, other triangles, special quadrilaterals, and polygons by composing into rectangles or decomposing into triangles and other shapes; apply these techniques to solve mathematical problems and problems in real-world context.

F8F840D5A6194776B6DC241A7DA64F5C.description: Solve mathematical problems and problems in real-world context involving area, surface area, and volume.

1D9B1D9A4E5D4F0C9078A4299CD3A378.description: Use variables to represent two quantities that change in relationship to one another to solve mathematical problems and problems in real-world context. Write an equation to express one quantity (the dependent variable) in terms of the other quantity (the independent variable). Analyze the relationship between the dependent and independent variables using graphs and tables, and relate these to the equation.

F25F9651EBB643B382DFC862A7C6527A.description: Represent and analyze quantitative relationships between dependent and independent variables.

B8A0043044774BA285949C9B4585B0DE.description: Write an inequality of the form x > c, x < c, x ≥ c, or x ≤ c to represent a constraint or condition to solve mathematical problems and problems in real-world context. Recognize that inequalities have infinitely many solutions; represent solutions of such inequalities on number lines.

E633900896AD401B92DFE92F28C9AA61.description: Solve mathematical problems and problems in real-world context by writing and solving equations of the form x + p = q, x - p = q, px = q, and x/p = q for cases in which p, q and x are all non-negative rational numbers.

04969671692542CFA82BB5153BD57D51.description: Use variables to represent numbers and write expressions when solving mathematical problems and problems in real-world context; understand that a variable can represent an unknown number or any number in a specified set.

9E73C01343F042B88D7545F3912D1249.description: Understand solving an equation or inequality as a process of reasoning to find the value(s) of the variables that make that equation or inequality true. Use substitution to determine whether a given number in a specified set makes an equation or inequality true.

A9727DBFD4834E83BEF3F3B1405659BD.description: Reason about and solve one-variable equations and inequalities.

DD4CDC105060448E9654206AB478A042.description: Identify when two expressions are equivalent.

D0ECC76243C14B62A073A0C24F3BFCE1.description: Apply the properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.

C647EF0CD6C34FC7B546A9EF00A6B232.description: Evaluate expressions given specific values of their variables. Include expressions that arise from formulas used to solve mathematical problems and problems in real-world context. Perform arithmetic operations, including those involving whole-number exponents, in the conventional order when there are no parentheses to specify a particular order (Order of Operations).

4885754E5FA443C6BCB043A45E78C180.description: Identify parts of an expression using mathematical terms (sum, term, product, factor, quotient, and coefficient); view one or more parts of an expression as a single entity.

C31B0134B7B54A628C4AC4E9E1BC0176.description: Write expressions that record operations with numbers and variables.

2DCB9BF1C1CB49B884605FEDC417AC49.description: Write, read, and evaluate algebraic expressions.

460F83D1B47A4E84BB95EA5CFD817882.description: Write and evaluate numerical expressions involving whole-number exponents.

A5C7866E68134100BF2DAFB167C2898B.description: Apply and extend previous understanding of arithmetic to algebraic expressions.

B47FD39F0B07450D9AD0D43E7F36CC19.description: Solve mathematical problems and problems in real-world context by graphing points in all four quadrants of the coordinate plane. Include use of coordinates and absolute value to find distances between points with the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate.

2E327242AC2C441CB24CA7C39B62B1EB.description: Distinguish comparisons of absolute value from statements about order in mathematical problems and problems in real-world context.

B438887DA19846B288A6335246B6DDE8.description: Understand the absolute value of a rational number as its distance from 0 on the number line; interpret absolute value as magnitude for a positive or negative quantity in real-world context.

C24496C65E0E430C82851145587A0244.description: Write, interpret, and explain statements of order for rational numbers in real-world context.

A308EE4F710348FEA1BFEDF598F0CB18.description: Interpret statements of inequality as statements about the relative position of two numbers on a number line.

ADF953935C0F4EE9A8F067C6600D26B6.description: Understand ordering and absolute value of rational numbers.

B51B51B904274DC292BCB74ED60CAE72.description: Find and position integers and other rational numbers on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram; find and position pairs of integers and other rational numbers on a coordinate plane.

58F854AA9EC54BBBB1CF2A6DAA1AE4CE.description: Understand signs of numbers in ordered pairs as indicating locations in quadrants of the coordinate plane; recognize that when two ordered pairs differ only by signs, the locations of the points are related by reflections across one or both axes.

F449320EC55143CD8528EBB4F476929D.description: Recognize opposite signs of numbers as indicating locations on opposite sides of 0 on the number line; recognize that the opposite of the opposite of a number is the number itself and that 0 is its own opposite.

E8ECD78C4387479D8BB4040DD9A359A2.description: Understand a rational number can be represented as a point on the number line. Extend number line diagrams and coordinate axes familiar from previous grades to represent points on the line and in the plane with negative number coordinates.

02F142531B214B31A3381A71BE9F3E24.description: Understand that positive and negative numbers are used together to describe quantities having opposite directions or values. Use positive and negative numbers to represent quantities in real-world context, explaining the meaning of 0 in each situation.

198F157FE2414FB2872A9BE36269E12A.description: Apply and extend previous understanding of numbers to the system of rational numbers.

F128836029ED43A3804F8B5E0BFAEEE5.description: Use the distributive property to express a sum of two whole numbers 1 to 100 with a common factor as a multiple of a sum of two whole numbers with no common factor. For example, express 36 + 8 as 4(9+2).

45F032F6A59B426FAE5E762A9D04A174.description: Find the least common multiple of two whole numbers less than or equal to 12.

F09B80B3C59744F8B3A5BDFE833F0D86.description: Find the greatest common factor of two whole numbers less than or equal to 100.

78129C77C3664B6C9F9CC1CB4C49D951.description: Use previous understanding of factors to find the greatest common factor and the least common multiple.

2A580BBE2E514859A8EB895292DD3766.description: Fluently add, subtract, multiply, and divide multi-digit decimals using a standard algorithm for each operation.

9DB9C24FAD26438582626FFE26C77FA3.description: Fluently divide multi-digit numbers using a standard algorithm.

78F78A260FC2403F83C7A74490CBA7CE.description: Compute fluently with multi-digit numbers and find common factors and multiples.

6DBDA8114665447CAB0F1BAAC49222CE.description: Interpret and compute quotients of fractions to solve mathematical problems and problems in real-world context involving division of fractions by fractions using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

8A0B40FDC45F48E28950D339175D3236.description: Apply and extend previous understanding of multiplication and division to divide fractions by fractions.

C6374BAE6E11432FB023079FD0EB0B7A.description: Use ratio reasoning to convert measurement units; manipulate and transform units appropriately when multiplying or dividing quantities.

B7A9A29C1ECD40B2A906A8EF1225F003.description: Find a percent of a quantity as a rate per 100 (e.g., 30% of a quantity means 30/100 times the quantity). Solve percent problems with the unknown in all positions of the equation.

005846920CB241C6B84E845912D047A1.description: Solve unit rate problems including those involving unit pricing and constant speed.

54C1F10289394FC6BDF78728A1A9812F.description: Make tables of equivalent ratios relating quantities with whole-number measurements, find missing values in the tables, and plot the pairs of values on the coordinate plane. Use tables to compare ratios.

FC84598D8573482BAD415E21268F258B.description: Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve mathematical problems and problems in real-world context (e.g., by reasoning about data collected from measurements, tables of equivalent ratios, tape diagrams, double number line diagrams, or equations).

668D7ACE1916438F9ADDB60C01B5F0CB.description: Understand the concept of a unit rate a/b associated with a ratio a : b with b ≠ 0, and use rate language (e.g., for every, for each, for each 1, per) in the context of a ratio relationship. (Complex fraction notation is not an expectation for unit rates in this grade level.)

82167EF40D1047418C68ED87ABD18E83.description: Understand the concept of a ratio as comparing two quantities multiplicatively or joining/composing the two quantities in a way that preserves a multiplicative relationship. Use ratio language to describe a ratio relationship between two quantities.

099275978F1D43AF813DACC710B615AC.description: Understand ratio concepts and use ratio reasoning to solve problems.

21127AF8C20A467B965327A870CE3F7B.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

5E9D225ACB9E495B868637120CDC4A03.description: Look for and make use of structure.

1E3FADC4ACA6403E8A6AF746108CE540.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

4C0E752D0DB64FCFB8BC6684B6D0B904.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

9B0CE63BE8F64691882D4BDD90408BDA.description: Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, thirds, fourths, half of, third of, fourth of, and describe the whole as two halves, three thirds, or four fourths. Recognize that equal shares of identical wholes need not have the same shape.

BD4A44FAE8F7468C81BB17EC21873895.description: Partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size rectangles and count to find the total number of rectangles.

90DC729DD14F4C4FAD2599BA695F443D.description: Identify and describe specified attributes of two-dimensional and three-dimensional shapes, according to the number and shape of faces, number of angles, and the number of sides and/or vertices. Draw two-dimensional shapes based on the specified attributes (e.g., triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, and hexagons).

284B7E43BF2341D4B8569E4858AEF442.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

39FD87C63855465EA300A47EDF5F48E7.description: Draw a picture graph and a bar graph (with single-unit scale) to represent a data set with up to four categories. Solve simple put-together, take-apart, and compare problems using information presented in the graph.

C85C510AD10E4D07BAC0E2FE1D113EE0.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths of several objects to the nearest whole unit, or by making repeated measurements of the same object. Show the measurements by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked off in whole-number units.

19D96648118B439784E9004679AFB9EB.description: Solve word problems involving collections of money, including dollar bills, quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies. Record the total using $ and ¢ appropriately.

A86BE3985F7A41FEAE7FE35C7741D98F.description: Tell and write time from analog and digital clocks to the nearest five minutes, using a.m. and p.m.

CCC758CECF904545AC677A49C9F54FD7.description: Represent whole numbers as lengths from 0 on a number line diagram with equally spaced points corresponding to the numbers 0, 1, 2, …, and represent whole-number sums and differences within 100 on a number line diagram.

25ADF4CD092648FBB0F2FFD826DE1BF5.description: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve word problems involving lengths that are given in the same unit.

671AFC759FBB4265B590F6CD8508E59C.description: Relate addition and subtraction to length.

C69600E6831144AB9F1C44148C8EE3A0.description: Measure to determine how much longer one object is than another, expressing the length difference in terms of a standard length unit.

3AA565CDCAC64DA49DC5CBEB6CB8511E.description: Estimate lengths using units of inches, feet, centimeters, and meters.

003A1D94485D4A7494FF42AA9DE8565A.description: Measure the length of an object twice, using different standard length units for the two measurements; describe how the two measurements relate to the size of the unit chosen. Understand that depending on the size of the unit, the number of units for the same length varies.

86E25CB4472C44D0AE057B3C4726BC28.description: Measure the length of an object by selecting and using appropriate tools (e.g., ruler, meter stick, yardstick, measuring tape).

784A1C09A09342A29369B92025DC053C.description: Measure and estimate lengths in standard units.

0414BCC8EA0C4D2FB71A8E7CE3230106.description: Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work, using place value and the properties of operations. (Explanations may be supported by drawings or objects.)

886DD41059E9400E9995313BB34E50D2.description: Mentally add 10 or 100 to a given number in the range of 100 and 900, and mentally subtract 10 or 100 from a given number in the range of 100 and 900.

AEE56087F7D54B0D8C1D645E166CDFA0.description: Demonstrate understanding of addition and subtraction within 1000, connecting objects or drawings to strategies based on place value (including multiples of 10), properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction. Relate the strategy to a written form.

A70E448F842041B8B7A5C94CE988B6E8.description: Add up to three two-digit numbers using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.

1195F93EE40C48B986D1EA866397C4D7.description: Fluently add and subtract within 100 using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.

48D2D568D8504BB6B7BC1719837C99EB.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.

F872642BB955427C8E01E5844C0DA3E6.description: Compare two three-digit numbers based on meanings of the hundreds, tens, and ones digits, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

AB5BD62493CD4A6EA5E518E5966E932A.description: Read and write numbers up to 1000 using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form.

C8F1CB5E319742408CF2263AA2BEA18D.description: Count within 1000; skip count by 5's, 10's and 100's.

DA7111EB178B480D9CCFBD4A28FEDA18.description: The numbers 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine hundreds (and 0 tens and 0 ones).

873260C3A7D84C09B6E043C9E0A9B03A.description: 100 can be thought of as a group of ten tens—called a "hundred."

BD98522750C445C6B449135304A41E86.description: Understand that the three digits of a three-digit number represent groups of hundreds, tens, and ones (e.g., 706 equals 7 hundreds, 0 tens, and 6 ones and also equals 70 tens and 6 ones). Understand the following as special cases:

05E3FBE552C64EC186027E08A4CA2D53.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

1A7EEC4615DF4899B48F7C927F56D26D.description: Use addition to find the total number of objects arranged in rectangular arrays (with up to 5 rows and 5 columns). Write an equation to express the total as a sum of equal addends.

66AF180ED3D64A0C8DA6E03776B0EA4C.description: Determine whether a group of objects (up to 20) has an odd or even number of members (e.g., by pairing objects or counting them by 2's).

DEB2CA9F6B7642ABB6E6229C1FBEEC9D.description: Work with equal groups of objects to gain foundations for multiplication.

E9DA2E73E9054C5F9AB44318055DD76E.description: Fluently add and subtract within 20. By the end of Grade 2, know from memory all sums of two one-digit numbers.

3AE3F51463DF482EABDB777EF4B47DDF.description: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve one-step word problems. Use addition to solve two-step word problems using single-digit addends. Represent a word problem as an equation with a symbol for the unknown.

E8FF3C98C9104B238B05B4C1EB3BA0A2.description: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.

E0F1F1DF590D43839E30FD2A150ABD02.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

7B77D90FA8B54A73BD20DB552459ECDF.description: Look for and make use of structure.

91F437D805ED45B4B3A15AFC231F10E2.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

F67E43501EEE49E6B86D3600E74F33E4.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

FE701018E907496DB1ADC5F1001903A1.description: Recognize a line of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure as a line across the figure such that the figure can be folded along the line into matching parts. Identify line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.

0C36E1B6ADD94870B5B2DB85FBB14C67.description: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size (e.g., understand right triangles as a category, and identify right triangles).

331A297EBC5644B0888BF3ED55537E43.description: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures.

BF804794AE9941B09667C4C5A63B0D7D.description: Draw and identify lines and angles, and classify shapes by properties of their lines and angles.

E7E4B5E332A14275BF1A0127C21D6C8B.description: Understand angle measures as additive. (When an angle is decomposed into non-overlapping parts, the angle measure of the whole is the sum of the angle measures of the parts.) Solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles on a diagram within mathematical problems as well as problems in real-world contexts.

CB290DF845144A3A870FF6AF069282A4.description: Measure angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor. Sketch angles of specified measure.

A2D82295F352488F9FD43DB68563D154.description: An angle that turns through n one-degree angles is said to have an angle measure of n degrees.

6FA980768AA44EC394CFDCB63895CD62.description: An angle is measured with reference to a circle with its center at the common endpoint of the rays, by considering the fraction of the circular arc between the points where the two rays intersect the circle. An angle that turns through 1/360 of a circle is called a "one-degree angle," and can be used to measure angles.

5A81FA564021482EA27CD058CEAE9D8D.description: Recognize angles as geometric shapes that are formed wherever two rays share a common endpoint, and understand concepts of angle measurement:

C4365D72F2BD43138FCED787E211D7AA.description: Geometric measurement: Understand concepts of angle and measure angles.

BC849682759344BABC98C299C2F65283.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (½, ¼, 1/8). Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions by using information presented in line plots.

409F7CF3207E48279E9B65F125D03041.description: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in mathematical problems and problems in real-world contexts including problems with unknown side lengths.

E6ED3791F4DE409BA41065B9B735A2B7.description: Use the four operations to solve word problems and problems in real-world context involving distances, intervals of time (hr, min, sec), liquid volumes, masses of objects, and money, including decimals and problems involving fractions with like denominators, and problems that require expressing measurements given in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Represent measurement quantities using a variety of representations, including number lines that feature a measurement scale.

19C4E6C184DF4A25BA0B7895FC636207.description: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system of units including km, m, cm; kg, g; lb, oz.; l, ml; hr, min, sec. Within a single system of measurement, express measurements in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit and in a smaller unit in terms of a larger unit.

2128F93EF754415CA9F42142842EED3E.description: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of measurements from a larger unit to a smaller unit.

AD72BD88508F42B6AC3970C75A13E3C5.description: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size. Understand that comparisons are valid only when the two decimals refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <.

77628EBF1BBD4F90B7139A0AEEAD15C0.description: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 (tenths) or 100 (hundredths), and locate these decimals on a number line.

F763C887536F463A98FE8A4264534E42.description: Express a fraction with denominator 10 as an equivalent fraction with denominator 100, and use this technique to add two fractions with respective denominators 10 (tenths) and 100 (hundredths).

EA5FF61BF6754FAD8F32CCD7203870EA.description: Understand decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal fractions.

6E7071F6DAF346C6A3F74E662BAFA44B.description: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a whole number by a fraction.

78BE906C965347E0B9F9061FED094650.description: Understand a multiple of a/b as a multiple of a unit fraction 1/b, and use this understanding to multiply a whole number by a fraction. In general, n × a/b = n × a/b.

1EF96943125D439C8042DFC459FFBF59.description: Understand a fraction a/b as a multiple of a unit fraction 1/b. In general, a/b = a × 1/b.

7596FC5962B0411D8DC44A0B11D55B59.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole and having like denominators.

639684FE10D84683A321E234D0A8AD51.description: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators (e.g., by using properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction and/or by replacing each mixed number with an equivalent fraction).

4159FF078BC34DD497AFF939D548C134.description: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way (e.g., 3/8 = 1/8 + 1/8 + 1/8; 3/8 = 2/8 + 1/8; 2 1/8 = 1 + 1 + 1/8 + or 2 1/8 = 8/8 + 8/8 + 1/8).

E83968EFADD24AEF8A7D226D423FEAB8.description: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole.

FC6AE17E4C804073BAB5B2FEDE6A422B.description: Understand a fraction a/b with a > 1 as a sum of unit fractions (1/b).

7AB1D70DDE234153A6548BA38BDC923A.description: Apply and extend previous understanding of multiplication to multiply a whole number by a fraction.

24B3016968864E1083EAA401FAA9348D.description: Record the results of comparisons with symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions.

4F2A4471A1524E4C86586CF90347C9D8.description: Understand that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same size whole.

D602F25AAC79412EA3FFA5C7AB414591.description: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators (e.g., by creating common denominators or numerators and by comparing to a benchmark fraction).

31EA1EFE891448D2A971EEE0A481976E.description: Explain why a fraction a/b is equivalent to a fraction (n × a)/(n × b) by using visual fraction models, with attention to how the number and size of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size. Use this principle to understand and generate equivalent fractions.

D8849E1D513441598FDFDA041307128A.description: Extend understanding of fraction equivalence and ordering.

4DEF24279F494E65B1AAF25156A4031C.description: Demonstrate understanding of division by finding whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors.

CBEEA1BAC0C6457BAB47DC7C44EAAACF.description: Multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit whole number, and multiply two two-digit numbers, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

12188A47642345CBB483C88A8061A1EC.description: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using a standard algorithm.

ECD968A7E2614BC58BA2DE75DFAB1A03.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

E65432036BE042648D1C2C95738211CC.description: Use place value understanding to round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.

038989B65AE94F14AE241FAE16A9E697.description: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form. Compare two multi-digit numbers based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

FCDC842F7EB5419ABF2EFD2116A6E3AF.description: Apply concepts of place value, multiplication, and division to understand that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right.

61533B7417284CE8BB40332DE0ECA7E4.description: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers.

B0213D54B733476FB8999129EE4B8B15.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

E1B58D06A6D843EEA685A5B31DE59A31.description: When solving problems, assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.

E6F205816A624B92B29EBD8FD0CD4EDE.description: Generate a number pattern that follows a given rule. Identify apparent features of the pattern that were not explicit in the rule itself and explain the pattern informally (e.g., given the rule "add 3" and the starting number 1, generate terms in the resulting sequence and observe that the terms appear to alternate between odd and even numbers).

D686790CDA5A425990DC68BC4859DD7A.description: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range 1 to 100 and understand that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors.

1323C3689C7245819E968CC63A332CC7.description: Gain familiarity with factors and multiples.

DC5531C3E439451C8B602EE4CFE84C92.description: Solve multi-step word problems using the four operations, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted. Understand how the remainder is a fraction of the divisor. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity.

3BACD69F143D49FB95D1A65B8F0D4228.description: Multiply or divide within 1000 to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison (e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem, distinguishing multiplicative comparison from additive comparison).

5871868DF76B464EBCB978615788BB38.description: Represent verbal statements of multiplicative comparisons as multiplication equations. Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison (e.g., 35 is the number of objects in 5 groups, each containing 7 objects, and is also the number of objects in 7 groups, each containing 5 objects).

37C5802DFF2541EB865C23284AC679BB.description: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems.

21C1772B1922488CBA86CF8B9510856F.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

B5A967E626EB48EE9EE98CB311DB254C.description: Look for and make use of structure.

81128D76693E4C04B9C5F83F909AB3F0.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

5967284067D648378F26BF8DC9C701F4.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

A9A99789E75941908E426BC4B96430E5.description: Use simple shapes to form composite shapes.

8985F85E66C9466188672219B674C9BC.description: Model shapes in the world by building shapes from components (e.g., use sticks and clay balls) and drawing shapes.

FBC2882F3DC14D65A0ABE63CA1CCEE6B.description: Analyze and compare two-dimensional and three-dimensional shapes, in different sizes and orientations, using informal language to describe their similarities, differences, parts (e.g., number of sides and vertices/corners), and other attributes (e.g., having sides of equal length).

5079407541D8477D8D99804509A38AF7.description: Analyze, compare, create, and compose shapes.

10CCFF4EB1344C4D9997B0BB2EAD49E1.description: Identify shapes as two-dimensional (lying in a plane, flat) or three-dimensional (solid).

ECAE9E57122449D984FA1FD10FAD5598.description: Correctly name shapes regardless of their orientation or overall size (e.g., circle, triangle, square, rectangle, rhombus, trapezoid, hexagon, cube, cone, cylinder, sphere).

D6D44F7931FA452AB0907079D7679981.description: Describe objects in the environment using names of shapes, and describe the relative positions of these objects using terms such as above, below, beside, in front of, behind, and next to.

5384D1CF037D497D9C10354EFEA6E588.description: Classify objects into given categories; count the number in each category and sort the categories by count. (Note: limit category counts to be less than or equal to 10.)

D1E87B11368E4C3AAD821FED7AE86F6A.description: Classify objects and count the number of objects in each category.

08FBC39DDBD54794B949F39C4EF33B8C.description: Directly compare two objects with a measurable attribute in common to see which object has "more of" or "less of" the attribute, and describe the difference (e.g., directly compare the length of 10 cubes to a pencil and describe one as longer or shorter).

04992F47172D4A25BBDD6AD6E552F494.description: Describe measurable attributes of a single object (e.g., length and weight).

7E02381E980941F4B36CBD8FDC5F1391.description: Demonstrate understanding of addition and subtraction within 10 using place value.

EAF09C3F0A524464B9FB17ABA12CEBE9.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.

AD4B2D83DFB94FD2953576F47C53C491.description: Compose and decompose numbers from 11 to 19 into ten ones and additional ones by using objects, drawings and/or equations. Understand that these numbers are composed of ten ones and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones (e.g., 18 = 10 + 8).

CB56DD03528F4A8CA2544EAEA2464B9F.description: Work with numbers 11 to 19 to gain foundations for place value.

256C2602A64B400F91AC617D82379232.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

15A6D6570E5A4EF4B723FED20B12E9CC.description: For any number from 1 to 9, find the number that makes 10 when added to the given number (e.g., using fingers, objects, symbols, tally marks, drawings, or equation).

122FAC7B98CB4044A5AF8E1704F2533E.description: Decompose numbers less than or equal to 10 into pairs in more than one way (e.g., using fingers, objects, symbols, tally marks, drawings, expressions).

9254F7607E9C47E99E96FB804F3F12CA.description: Solve addition and subtraction word problems and add and subtract within 10.

4F8A57A9C9DA4DA0BC0E2ED0B3A08D6A.description: Understand addition as putting together and adding to, and understand subtraction as taking apart and taking from.

5F105FCDAA3B4C029A73596996181276.description: Compare two numbers between 0 and 10 presented as written numerals.

AB42D456F1B24A88B04BC7300D287AF2.description: Identify whether the number of objects in one group is greater than, less than, or equal to the number of objects in another group. (Include groups with up to ten objects.)

783B29D0D43B4D0097532E9AB43B6659.description: Count to answer questions about "How many?" when 20 or fewer objects are arranged in a line, a rectangular array, or a circle, or as many as 10 things in a scattered configuration; given a number from 1 to 20, count out that many objects.

8F12B0447DF94ECAB2EB4D2F5B44AB12.description: Understand that each successive number name refers to a quantity that is one larger (hierarchical inclusion).

DB58A22FDEDE4A0C9DD5F8EB43907A59.description: Understand that the last number name said tells the number of objects counted. The number of objects is the same regardless of their arrangement or the order in which they were counted (cardinality).

C5DBBEAFFC7A4978953C230EBDCDB71D.description: When counting objects, say the number names in the standard order, pairing each object with one and only one number name and each number name with one and only one object (one to one correspondence).

CDA78A85013546C6B7255666C27A366E.description: Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities; connect counting to cardinality.

B09FCE3B59384958AA5E41DB7EC1E8D5.description: Count to tell the number of objects.

7FE6541976424E7D8C1471AB9952C949.description: Write numbers from 0 to 20. Represent a number of objects with a written numeral 0 to 20 (with 0 representing a count of no objects).

B188D87270814AD39995BB5A0C49788E.description: Count forward from a given number other than one, within the known sequence (e.g., "Starting at the number 5, count up to 11.").

BA1ABE2E108E45FF9D9751E84918E5E0.description: Count to 100 by ones and by tens.

B66EEBE62FFE48479F53BD0546FD04F3.description: Know number names and the count sequence.

23974C8B3C2E40F083AD78FB36D1AA5A.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

2965D657A36A4F088D6B7D64677B138D.description: Look for and make use of structure.

842AE4444EB9455F9CB1ABDE9D0BCC58.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

ACC1F6D71CBF456BB367FD76294C4635.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

66BB44BCD2CF4896917B42A9B66C28B1.description: Partition shapes into b parts with equal areas. Express the area of each part as a unit fraction 1/b of the whole. (Grade 3 expectations are limited to fractions with denominators b = 2, 3, 4, 6, 8.)

223A78C0FE33470889077F77DD0DA588.description: Understand that shapes in different categories (e.g., rhombuses, rectangles, and others)may share attributes (e.g., having four sides), and that the shared attributes can define a larger category (e.g., quadrilaterals). Recognize rhombuses, rectangles, and squares as examples of quadrilaterals, and draw examples quadrilaterals that do not belong to any of these subcategories.

38E9ECDBC86941E6A7350472302FC615.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

9CE53D4B3E094F4F8DD73377A5B584C5.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving perimeters of plane figures and areas of rectangles, including finding the perimeter given the side lengths, finding an unknown side length. Represent rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas or with the same area and different perimeters.

EAB5B44CD79244DA8B827FBB943AD9F8.description: Understand that rectilinear figures can be decomposed into non-overlapping rectangles and that the sum of the areas of these rectangles is identical to the area of the original rectilinear figure. Apply this technique to solve problems in real-world contexts.

DDA4E5381E8B4CEAA4E713F497ADFBA3.description: Use tiling to show that the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths a and b + c is the sum of a × b and a × c. Use area models to represent the distributive property in mathematical reasoning.

64320CEACE934EB4AFE3BE5CFC69C21D.description: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole-number side lengths in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematical reasoning.

92090C773717403E8E808E62BEB1D4DD.description: Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by tiling it, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths.

97144E3ABB3D49F4A0FDBD613B62D64F.description: Relate area to the operations of multiplication and addition.

5C5F2073F51249589C69C3A6CB476D0E.description: Measure areas by counting unit squares (e.g., square cm, square m, square in, square ft, and improvised units).

656913E3B66C488AB7334029CA0FF1D4.description: A plane figure which can be covered without gaps or overlaps by n unit squares is said to have an area of n square units.

F24E689EA0EE4D4B9F653C400C4F0F50.description: A square with side length 1 unit, called "a unit square," is said to have "one square unit" of area, and can be used to measure area.

8704E456EE2145918E33408C5F93391A.description: Understand area as an attribute of plane figures and understand concepts of area measurement.

359CCC1F7F324852948693853D1F3214.description: Geometric measurement: Understand concepts of area and perimeter.

BDB16FE23762478989EBD24A8CEC6659.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths using rulers marked with halves and fourths of an inch to the nearest quarter-inch. Show the data by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked off in appropriate units— whole numbers, halves, or quarters.

88BF106640094E288299B7FBB43D4F2A.description: Create a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set with several categories. Solve one- and two-step "how many more" and "how many less" problems using information presented in scaled bar graphs.

76E995D2C4554F2DBA1A0ACAA8175465.description: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses of objects using metric units. (Excludes compound units such as cm3 and finding the geometric volume of a container.) Add, subtract, multiply, or divide to solve one-step word problems involving masses or volumes that are given in the same units. Excludes multiplicative comparison problems (problems involving notions of "times as much").

F139080651D94A439DB76CF237C09F0C.description: Solve word problems involving money through $20.00, using symbols $, ".", ₵.

6895D39BC9E64C818B27FCBE2B8EE1DE.description: Tell and write time to the nearest minute and measure time intervals in minutes. Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals in minutes (e.g., representing the problem on a number line diagram).

AD7ED28F4A1F40B0A1EA4567124A235F.description: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator by reasoning about their size. Understand that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <, and justify conclusions.

DEA39F0E3D3A46FAAFDA7AEEF302FB59.description: Express whole numbers as fractions, and recognize fractions that are equivalent to whole numbers.

4421E98915F249BE871E8B2005641DFF.description: Recognize and generate simple equivalent fractions. Explain why the fractions are equivalent.

E33A708110C6401AAA84142F4CD34CDC.description: Understand two fractions as equivalent if they have the same relative size compared to 1 whole.

3A6EE359A6554AA49D2C0BF94FDB5DBE.description: Explain equivalence of fractions in special cases, and compare fractions by reasoning about their size.

B5C9BD92A81F432AB325BA68F2B167AE.description: Understand a fraction 1/b as a special type of fraction that can be referred to as a unit fraction (e.g. ½, ¼).

20B438F08EF04303A7DD7819BAB77DA7.description: Represent a fraction a/b on a number line diagram by marking off a lengths 1/b from 0. Understand that the resulting interval has size a/b and that its endpoint locates the number a/b on the number line including values greater than 1.

547238BBF27D43CFA8C5F83E8962BB31.description: Represent a fraction 1/b on a number line diagram by defining the interval from 0 to 1 as the whole and partitioning it into b equal parts. Understand that each part has size 1/b and that the end point of the part based at 0 locates the number 1/b on the number line.

5D9128C7E8454211B8F56EF830991F20.description: Understand a fraction as a number on the number line; represent fractions on a number line diagram.

1553B9B3E787427FB674E01F5542C4A4.description: Understand a fraction (1/b) as the quantity formed by one part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts; understand a fraction a/b as the quantity formed by a parts of size 1/b.

832CA9F5888842E680993BCBD1386168.description: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of 10 in the range 10 to 90 using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations (e.g., 9 × 80, 5 × 60).

FDD02D7AFB9B452E8FE3D16C0823BC75.description: Fluently add and subtract within 1000 using strategies and algorithms based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.

F3499DD3D36B4914827AF6E330E81255.description: Use place value understanding to round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.

50FED795D38C4BAE96356884F1E5EE98.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

06DC2F42800C45A3848C8FC647535041.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

0C6CFB18DAAE4C5DA21CEBFEA962F49E.description: When solving problems, assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.

EBEE3376B78C4B9396001F0FAB2E9AA3.description: Identify patterns in the addition table and the multiplication table and explain them using properties of operations (e.g. observe that 4 times a number is always even, and explain why 4 times a number can be decomposed into two equal addends).

0D1ED0CFC22A460ABA0E3745B944DD65.description: Solve two-step word problems using the four operations. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Utilize understanding of the Order of Operations when there are no parentheses.

F9A52917F5B1455AA386637AEE14DA0C.description: Solve problems involving the four operations, and identify and explain patterns in arithmetic.

DC519005C5BD4A08A0EA27BD65733AD5.description: Fluently multiply and divide within 100. By the end of Grade 3, know from memory all multiplication products through 10 × 10 and division quotients when both the quotient and divisor are less than or equal to 10.

45E69FFDF3794B09A4AA9875F625AE0A.description: Understand division as an unknown-factor problem (e.g., find 32 ÷ 8 by finding the number that makes 32 when multiplied by 8).

A0D79DAB6EF4464D9D5BB1250E0DCA12.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide. Properties include commutative and associative properties of multiplication and the distributive property. (Students do not need to use the formal terms for these properties.)

B1FB60231B274B3BB1EEAFE724224644.description: Understand properties of multiplication and the relationship between multiplication and division.

C4D6761713984B6DA92C48BAC6A5DEEA.description: Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation relating three whole numbers For example, determine the unknown number that makes the equation true in each of the equations 8 × ? = 48, 5 = ? ÷ 3, 6 × 6 = ?.

DA15F4F240144694BD9DD4E29CC50B80.description: Use multiplication and division within 100 to solve word problems in situations involving equal groups, arrays, and measurement quantities.

3BA7B7061C4D408FA62380A0DD9942A4.description: Interpret whole number quotients of whole numbers (e.g., interpret 56 ÷ 8 as the number of objects in each group when 56 objects are partitioned equally into 8 groups, or as a number of groups when 56 objects are partitioned into equal groups of 8 objects each).

FB04A58B7E2542C0AD90AA4A06F5DEA8.description: Interpret products of whole numbers as the total number of objects in equal groups (e.g., interpret 5 × 7 as the total number of objects in 5 groups of 7 objects each).

7711986E656C4C70991401D42376B9B9.description: Represent and solve problems involving whole number multiplication and division.

A6D1961D627A45D18A03AEE3262C3D60.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

561F02EFF46147BE9A5768337F2DEC0A.description: Look for and make use of structure.

765C77BB10E74732AF3252619857EF71.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

ACCD07909F964EE894B2EB8B7CC5E2EE.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

328664BE984A449E861B80DF0A475474.description: Develop a probability model (which may not be uniform) by observing frequencies in data generated from a chance process.

CA4A0DA9AF014839A3CA37590F453378.description: Develop a uniform probability model by assigning equal probability to all outcomes, and use the model to determine probabilities of events.

C3B7D05EC1E2430D9E30C240BAFCC959.description: Develop a probability model and use it to find probabilities of events. Compare probabilities from a model to observed frequencies. If the agreement is not good, explain possible sources of the discrepancy.

88DB7F41F1A24912A434818CB7DAB6D0.description: Approximate the probability of a chance event by collecting data on the chance process that produces it and observing its long-run relative frequency, and predict the approximate relative frequency given the probability.

E5F9CBFC1E0C4463B68701C3D6B40559.description: Understand that the probability of a chance event is a number between 0 and 1 that expresses the likelihood of the event occurring. Larger numbers indicate greater likelihood. A probability near 0 indicates an unlikely event, a probability around 1/2 indicates an event that is neither unlikely nor likely, and a probability near 1 indicates a likely event.

6169B91843074041B9282B8E83203125.description: Investigate chance processes and develop, use and evaluate probability models.

87E3C338294D4C8396D687825E50683F.description: Use measures of center and measures of variability for numerical data from random samples to draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.

928B820BF9C348398039CC8050590A33.description: Informally assess the degree of visual overlap of two numerical data distributions with similar variabilities, measuring the difference between the centers by expressing it as a multiple of a measure of variability.

2BCA59F79C174E1AAFAB2D9589E5FDDC.description: Draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.

AEF14D6471674226A5D8CE2877898923.description: Use data from a random sample to draw inferences about a population with an unknown characteristic of interest. Generate multiple samples (or simulated samples) of the same size to gauge the variation in estimates or predictions.

436ABB39F59449999F2F3F70ECC1CD8C.description: Understand that statistics can be used to gain information about a population by examining a sample of the population; generalizations about a population from a sample are valid only if the sample is representative of that population. Understand that random sampling tends to produce representative samples and support valid inferences.

BC6F633D5FF04A3D954A36E3EB2E9260.description: Use random sampling to draw inferences about a population.

A1F55140C8674DD8A861702D6A442831.description: Solve mathematical problems and problems in a real-world context involving area, of two-dimensional objects composed of triangles, quadrilaterals, and other polygons. Solve mathematical problems and problems in real-world context involving volume and surface area of three-dimensional objects composed of cubes and right prisms.

88E73F1BB53C477A9FFE888D9B9864AA.description: Use facts about supplementary, complementary, vertical, and adjacent angles in multi-step problems to write and solve simple equations for an unknown angle in a figure.

04C02C69907D4F5B9B28AEAF02CF334D.description: Understand and use the formulas for the area and circumference of a circle to solve problems; give an informal derivation of the relationship between the circumference and area of a circle.

FBE703087E7A44739A021CDCA411113E.description: Solve mathematical problems and problems in real-world context involving angle measure, area, surface area, and volume.

DA87EAAD517248D9853AF971A5463E8C.description: Describe the two-dimensional figures that result from slicing three-dimensional figures.

DD9988A3543442B398B77AE4B000ECB6.description: Draw geometric shapes with given conditions using a variety of methods. Focus on constructing triangles from three measures of angles or sides, noticing when the conditions determine a unique triangle, more than one triangle, or no triangle.

C5837603942148328D741E29F5435EDB.description: Solve problems involving scale drawings of geometric figures, such as computing actual lengths and areas from a scale drawing and reproducing a scale drawing at a different scale.

DC289F4413554A868C5D78849FF7BD28.description: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures, and describe the relationships between them.

DCECEA57687C4B9EBD9EBBF930BEF824.description: Solve word problems leading to inequalities of the form px + q > r or px + q < r, where p, q, and r are rational numbers. Graph the solution set of the inequality and interpret it in the context of the problem.

CCA72EBA3554429183AD1284150BBAB6.description: Solve word problems leading to equations of the form px + q = r and p(x + q) = r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Solve equations of these forms fluently. Compare an algebraic solution to an arithmetic solution, identifying the sequence of the operations used in each approach.

58269200182D45D39A1DF1C275B4E457.description: Use variables to represent quantities in mathematical problems and problems in real-world context, and construct simple equations and inequalities to solve problems.

BD395D48771043A4B81AD5393D66EF46.description: Solve multi-step mathematical problems and problems in real-world context posed with positive and negative rational numbers in any form. Convert between forms as appropriate and assess the reasonableness of answers.

E602BBE0DA084CD5903A0E11D7BA7F6A.description:
Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
Mathematically proficient students look for and describe regularities as they solve multiple related problems. They formulate conjectures about
what they notice and communicate observations with precision. While solving problems, students maintain oversight of the process and
continually evaluate the reasonableness of their results. This informs and strengthens their understanding of the structure of mathematics which
leads to fluency.

4ABD7F650ACF454CB50D4874FE241F58.description:
Look for and make use of structure.
Mathematically proficient students use structure and patterns to assist in making connections among mathematical ideas or concepts when
making sense of mathematics. Students recognize and apply general mathematical rules to complex situations. They are able to compose and
decompose mathematical ideas and notations into familiar relationships. Mathematically proficient students manage their own progress, stepping
back for an overview and shifting perspective when needed.

9D85F5D3DF83416E9BBBA9EFC57B5354.description:
Attend to precision.
Mathematically proficient students clearly communicate to others using appropriate mathematical terminology, and craft explanations that convey
their reasoning. When making mathematical arguments about a solution, strategy, or conjecture, they describe mathematical relationships and
connect their words clearly to their representations. Mathematically proficient students understand meanings of symbols used in mathematics,
calculate accurately and efficiently, label quantities appropriately, and record their work clearly and concisely.

041E26D186EC48978219FCB95EEDDE98.description: Use appropriate tools strategically. Mathematically proficient students consider available tools when solving a mathematical problem. They choose tools that are relevant and useful to the problem at hand. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful; recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. Students deepen their understanding of mathematical concepts when using tools to visualize, explore, compare, communicate, make and test predictions, and understand the thinking of others.

66A7E500CCBD4A4C88236C9DEB475876.description: Model with mathematics. Mathematically proficient students apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. When given a problem in a contextual situation, they identify the mathematical elements of a situation and create a mathematical model that represents those mathematical elements and the relationships among them. Mathematically proficient students use their model to analyze the relationships and draw conclusions. They interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

F04E680464674972BE687EB2D50D1F41.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others. Mathematically proficient students construct mathematical arguments (explain the reasoning underlying a strategy, solution, or conjecture) using concrete, pictorial, or symbolic referents. Arguments may also rely on definitions, assumptions, previously established results, properties, or structures. Mathematically proficient students make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. Mathematically proficient students present their arguments in the form of representations, actions on those representations, and explanations in words (oral or written). Students critique others by affirming or questioning the reasoning of others. They can listen to or read the reasoning of others, decide whether it makes sense, ask questions to clarify or improve the reasoning, and validate or build on it. Mathematically proficient students can communicate their arguments, compare them to others, and reconsider their own arguments in response to the critiques of others.

AA9C2238CD354475A86B561C96C548A6.description: Reason abstractly and quantitatively. Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. Students can contextualize and decontextualize problems involving quantitative relationships. They contextualize quantities, operations, and expressions by describing a corresponding situation. They decontextualize a situation by representing it symbolically. As they manipulate the symbols, they can pause as needed to access the meaning of the numbers, the units, and the operations that the symbols represent. Mathematically proficient students know and flexibly use different properties of operations, numbers, and geometric objects and when appropriate they interpret their solution in terms of the context.

428430C83588464A8363BD42D375AD0A.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them. Mathematically proficient students explain to themselves the meaning of a problem, look for entry points to begin work on the problem, and plan and choose a solution pathway. While engaging in productive struggle to solve a problem, they continually ask themselves, “Does this make sense?" to monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Once they have a solution, they look back at the problem to determine if the solution is reasonable and accurate. Mathematically proficient students check their solutions to problems using different methods, approaches, or representations. They also compare and understand different representations of problems and different solution pathways, both their own and those of others.
